The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $A\in GL_3(\mathbb R)$, let $\Lambda=A\mathbb Z^3$, let
$V=|\det A|$, and let $\mathbb T_A=\mathbb R^3/\Lambda$. These are the
full-rank lattice and covolume conventions of
[[def-full-rank-lattice-covolume-and-dual-lattice]]. The reciprocal lattice is
$\Lambda^*=A^{-T}\mathbb Z^3$. For $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ write
$$\kappa_k=2\pi A^{-T}k,\qquad e_k(x)=e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}.$$
Thus $e_k$ is a character of $\mathbb T_A$; the ordinary Fourier frequency is
$A^{-T}k$, while $\kappa_k$ is the angular physical frequency.

A finite point-source configuration consists of an integer $n\ge0$, points
$x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb T_A$ that are pairwise distinct when $n>1$, and
real charges $q_1,\ldots,q_n$. It is **neutral** when
$\sum_{i=1}^n q_i=0$. For a smooth periodic test function $\varphi$, the
point-source distribution is the linear functional
$$\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^nq_i\varphi(x_i).$$
Here smooth means that the periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$ has continuous
derivatives of every order, and the test-function topology is generated by the
seminorms $\max_{x\in A[0,1]^3}|\partial^\beta\varphi(x)|$ over all derivative
multi-indices $\beta$. A periodic distribution is a continuous complex-linear
functional for this topology. Its distributional Laplacian is defined by
$\langle-\Delta u,\varphi\rangle=\langle u,-\Delta\varphi\rangle$.

For a smooth periodic $\varphi$, its Fourier coefficient is
$$\widehat\varphi(k)=\frac1V\int_{A(0,1]^3}\varphi(x)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\,dx.$$
The source coefficient is
$$\widehat\rho(k)=\frac1V\sum_{i=1}^nq_i e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i};$$
in particular, neutral data have $\widehat\rho(0)=0$. For a periodic
distribution $u$, define $\widehat u(k)=V^{-1}\langle u,e_{-k}\rangle$. The
**mean-zero periodic Poisson solution** is a periodic distribution $u$ satisfying
$-\Delta u=4\pi\rho$ and $\widehat u(0)=0$. This definition fixes the
zero-mode convention; no nonneutral periodic solution is implicit.

The Coulomb energy convention is the half-sum of each source charge times the
regular part of its potential, after subtracting its own singular term
$q_i/|x-x_i|$. The resulting finite part is called the **renormalized
self-energy convention**. Its Ewald formula is established in this development.

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite point-source data
$(A,V,\Lambda,\kappa_k,(x_i,q_i)_{i=1}^n)$ from
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]], with pairwise distinct
source positions in $\mathbb T_A$. For $\alpha>0$ put
$$\sigma_k=\sum_iq_i e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i},\qquad c_k(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi}{V|\kappa_k|^2}e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}\quad(k\ne0).$$
For every off-source point $x\notin\bigcup_i(x_i+\Lambda)$, the absolutely
convergent Ewald potential
$$U_\alpha(x)=\sum_iq_i\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda} \frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha|x-x_i+\lambda|)}{|x-x_i+\lambda|} +\frac{4\pi}{V}\sum_{k\ne0}\frac{e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}}{|\kappa_k|^2} \sigma_k e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}$$
is the off-source representative of the unique mean-zero periodic solution of
$-\Delta u=4\pi\rho$. Hence it is independent of $\alpha$.

Define the regular part at $x_i$ by
$$\operatorname{FP}_{x_i}U_\alpha= \lim_{x\to x_i}\left(U_\alpha(x)-\frac{q_i}{|x-x_i|}\right).$$
The limit exists, is independent of $\alpha$, and the renormalized energy is
$$E=\frac12\sum_iq_i\operatorname{FP}_{x_i}U_\alpha =\frac12\sum_i\sum_{(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0)}q_iq_j \frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha|x_i-x_j+\lambda|)} {|x_i-x_j+\lambda|} +\frac12\sum_{k\ne0}c_k(\alpha)|\sigma_k|^2 -\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\sum_iq_i^2.$$
The prime-exclusion written as $(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0)$ omits only each particle's
own zero-image singularity.

Use the periodic cardinal-assignment model of
[[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]], with integers $M_r\ge1$, order
$P\ge2$, grid size $N_g=\prod_rM_r$, a retained signed mode $k$ satisfying
$|k_r|<M_r/2$, and $D(k)\ne0$. Put $u_r=k_r/M_r$,
$a_k(t)=e^{-2\pi i k\cdot t}$, and
$$r_{k,n}=\prod_{r=1}^3 \frac{\overline{D_r(k_r+n_rM_r)}}{\overline{D_r(k_r)}},\qquad D_r(m)=e^{-\pi iPm/M_r}\operatorname{sinc}(\pi m/M_r)^P.$$
Then the single-particle assignment factor and the spread-grid coefficient obey
the absolutely convergent identities
$$b_k(t)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}r_{k,n}a_{k+n\odot M}(t),\qquad z_k=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}r_{k,n}\rho_{k+n\odot M},$$
where $(n\odot M)_r=n_rM_r$ and
$\rho_j=\sum_iq_i e^{-2\pi i j\cdot t_i}$. In particular
$$z_k-\rho_k=\sum_{n\ne0}r_{k,n}\rho_{k+n\odot M}.$$
The mesh coefficient also has the exact finite representation
$z_k=\sum_iq_i b_k(t_i)$, so no cell-volume or grid-size factor remains after
the displayed $\sqrt{N_g}$ conversion. The alias bound below uses only the Fourier series of
the compact spline; the lattice Poisson theorem is not applied to that spline.

For $u_r\ne0$ define
$$a_r(P,u_r)=\sum_{m\ne0}\left|\frac{u_r}{u_r+m}\right|^P, \qquad a_r(P,0)=0,\qquad A_k=\prod_{r=1}^3(1+a_r(P,u_r))-1.$$
Then $|b_k(t)-a_k(t)|\le A_k$, $|b_k(t)|\le1+A_k$, and
$|z_k-\rho_k|\le Q A_k$ for $Q=\sum_i|q_i|$. For $J\ge1$ and
$0<|u_r|<1/2$,
$$a_r(P,u_r)\le 2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\sum_{m=1}^\infty m^{-P},\qquad \sum_{|m|>J}\left|\frac{u_r}{u_r+m}\right|^P\le 2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\frac{\lfloor J\rfloor^{1-P}}{P-1}.$$
Thus every alias controller has a finite p-series remainder bound.
The periodic assignment also satisfies $\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t)=1$,
so the spread-grid zero mode is $\sum_{\ell}g_\ell=\sum_iq_i=0$ for neutral data.

Fix neutral point-source data $(A,V,\Lambda,\kappa_k,(x_i,q_i)_{i=1}^n)$ from
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]], an Ewald parameter
$\alpha>0$, integers $M_1,M_2,M_3\ge1$, an assignment order $P\ge2$, and write
$N_g=M_1M_2M_3$. Let $\mathcal G=\prod_{r=1}^3\{0,\ldots,M_r-1\}$ and take
$W_P$ from [[def-ewald-causal-cardinal-spline-window]]. Define the periodic
causal assignment weights, for $t\in[0,1)^3$ and $\ell\in\mathcal G$, by
$$w_\ell(t)=\prod_{r=1}^3\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z} W_P(M_rt_r-\ell_r-jM_r).$$
The sums are finite because $W_P$ is supported on $[0,P]$. They collect every
support index into its grid residue; if $P>M_r$, distinct support indices that
wrap to the same residue are added. The spread grid is
$$g_\ell=\sum_{i=1}^n q_iw_\ell(t_i),\qquad t_i=A^{-1}x_i\pmod{\mathbb Z^3}.$$

Use the negative-sign unitary tensor DFT convention
$$\widehat g_M(k)=N_g^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}g_\ell e^{-2\pi i\sum_{r=1}^3k_r\ell_r/M_r},$$
which is the product transform of
[[def-unitary-discrete-fourier-transform-on-z-mod-n]]. Signed frequency
representatives are chosen before evaluating windows. A retained set
$\mathcal K\subset\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$ is finite, symmetric under
$k\mapsto-k$, injective modulo $(M_1,M_2,M_3)$, and satisfies
$|k_r|<M_r/2$ for each coordinate. In particular, even-grid Nyquist modes are
not silently retained.

For $u\in\mathbb R$, put $\operatorname{sinc}(u)=\sin(u)/u$ when $u\ne0$ and
$\operatorname{sinc}(0)=1$. Define
$$D(k)=\prod_{r=1}^3e^{-\pi iPk_r/M_r} \operatorname{sinc}(\pi k_r/M_r)^P.$$
Only modes with $D(k)\ne0$ are admissible for division. A computed
implementation must first certify a strictly positive lower bound for
$|D(k)|$; otherwise it returns `denominator-inconclusive` without dividing.
For $k\in\mathcal K$, define
$$a_k(t)=e^{-2\pi i k\cdot t},\quad b_k(t)=\frac{\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t) e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}}{\overline{D(k)}},\quad \rho_k=\sum_iq_i a_k(t_i),\quad z_k=\frac{\sqrt{N_g}\,\widehat g_M(k)}{\overline{D(k)}}.$$
The denominator is the complex conjugate of the printed window multiplier; this
sign is part of the definition. Set
$$c_k=\frac{4\pi}{V|\kappa_k|^2} e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}.$$
The exact retained reciprocal energy is
$$E_{\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|\rho_k|^2,$$
and the mesh reciprocal energy is
$$E_M=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|z_k|^2.$$

Let $\mathfrak d_k(t)$ be the declared physical mesh derivative: it is
$\nabla_xb_k(t)=A^{-T}\nabla_tb_k(t)$ wherever the classical derivative
exists. A grid knot is a point with $M_rt_r\in\mathbb Z$ for some coordinate
$r$. At a $P=2$ knot, take the one-sided vector limits from all adjacent open
mesh boxes. Define $\mathfrak d_k(t)$ to be any selected one-sided limit or the
arithmetic average of all those limits. This is a procedure value and does not
assert that the classical derivative exists there. The
energy-gradient mesh force is
$$F_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\overline{z_k}\mathfrak d_k(t_i)\right).$$
Define the diagonal mesh-self correction and corrected reciprocal energy by
$$C_M=\frac12\sum_iq_i^2\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k (|b_k(t_i)|^2-1),\qquad E_M^{\mathrm{corr}}=E_M-C_M.$$
Whether the declared force is the derivative of this corrected energy, and the
error bound it satisfies, are proved separately.

Use the data and aliases of
[[lem-ewald-pme-spline-alias-and-dft-normalization]]. Write
$h_r(0)=1$ and, for $u_r=k_r/M_r\ne0$,
$h_r(n)=|u_r/(u_r+n)|^P$ for $n\ne0$; when $u_r=0$, set $h_r(n)=0$ for
$n\ne0$. Put
$$a_r=\sum_{n\ne0}h_r(n).$$
For $P\ge3$, define
$$v_r=\sum_{n\ne0}|k_r+nM_r|h_r(n),\qquad J_{k,r}=(|k_r|+v_r)\prod_{s\ne r}(1+a_s)-|k_r|,$$
and
$$B_k=2\pi\|A^{-T}\|_2\left(\sum_{r=1}^3J_{k,r}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
For $P\ge3$ the physical derivative alias error satisfies
$$\|\nabla_xb_k(t)-\nabla_xa_k(t)\|_2\le B_k.$$
Each series has a finite p-series controller: for $0<|u_r|<1/2$,
$$a_r\le2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\zeta(P),\qquad v_r\le2M_r\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^{P-1}}\zeta(P-1),$$
where $\zeta(s)=\sum_{m\ge1}m^{-s}$ for $s>1$. For $J_0\ge1$, after summing exactly over
$1\le|n|\le J_0$, the respective omitted tails are at most

$V=|\det A|$, and let $\mathbb T_A=\mathbb R^3/\Lambda$. These are the
full-rank lattice and covolume conventions of
[[def-full-rank-lattice-covolume-and-dual-lattice]]. The reciprocal lattice is
$\Lambda^*=A^{-T}\mathbb Z^3$. For $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ write
$$\kappa_k=2\pi A^{-T}k,\qquad e_k(x)=e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}.$$
Thus $e_k$ is a character of $\mathbb T_A$; the ordinary Fourier frequency is
$A^{-T}k$, while $\kappa_k$ is the angular physical frequency.

A finite point-source configuration consists of an integer $n\ge0$, points
$x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb T_A$ that are pairwise distinct when $n>1$, and
real charges $q_1,\ldots,q_n$. It is **neutral** when
$\sum_{i=1}^n q_i=0$. For a smooth periodic test function $\varphi$, the
point-source distribution is the linear functional
$$\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^nq_i\varphi(x_i).$$
Here smooth means that the periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$ has continuous
derivatives of every order, and the test-function topology is generated by the
seminorms $\max_{x\in A[0,1]^3}|\partial^\beta\varphi(x)|$ over all derivative
multi-indices $\beta$. A periodic distribution is a continuous complex-linear
functional for this topology. Its distributional Laplacian is defined by
$\langle-\Delta u,\varphi\rangle=\langle u,-\Delta\varphi\rangle$.

For a smooth periodic $\varphi$, its Fourier coefficient is
$$\widehat\varphi(k)=\frac1V\int_{A(0,1]^3}\varphi(x)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\,dx.$$
The source coefficient is
$$\widehat\rho(k)=\frac1V\sum_{i=1}^nq_i e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i};$$
in particular, neutral data have $\widehat\rho(0)=0$. For a periodic
distribution $u$, define $\widehat u(k)=V^{-1}\langle u,e_{-k}\rangle$. The
**mean-zero periodic Poisson solution** is a periodic distribution $u$ satisfying
$-\Delta u=4\pi\rho$ and $\widehat u(0)=0$. This definition fixes the
zero-mode convention; no nonneutral periodic solution is implicit.

The Coulomb energy convention is the half-sum of each source charge times the
regular part of its potential, after subtracting its own singular term
$q_i/|x-x_i|$. The resulting finite part is called the **renormalized
self-energy convention**. Its Ewald formula is established in this development.

The functions $\sin$ and $\cos$ are differentiable on $\mathbb R$, with
$$(\sin x)'=\cos x,\qquad(\cos x)'=-\sin x.$$
Also $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$.

Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g[A] \subseteq B$ and let $f : B \to \mathbb{R}$, so that the composite
$f \circ g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined. Let $c \in A$ be a limit point of
$A$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]) at which $g$ is differentiable
([[def-derivative]]), put $b := g(c)$, and suppose $b$ is a limit point of $B$
at which $f$ is differentiable. Then $f \circ g$ is differentiable at $c$ and

$$(f \circ g)'(c) \;=\; f'\bigl(g(c)\bigr)\,g'(c) .$$

is a limit point of $A$ is what makes $g'(c)$ and $(f \circ g)'(c)$ defined
symbols; that $b = g(c)$ is a limit point of $B$ is what makes $f'(b)$ one.
Nothing forces the second: $g$ may be differentiable at $c$ and send $c$ to an
isolated point of $B$, and there $f'(b)$ is not defined and the formula asserts
nothing.

**No case analysis appears anywhere.** The naive difference-quotient proof
writes $\frac{f(g(x)) - f(g(c))}{g(x) - g(c)} \cdot \frac{g(x) - g(c)}{x - c}$
and then has to say what happens where $g(x) = g(c)$, which may occur at points
arbitrarily close to $c$. Carathéodory's factorisation never divides by the
inner increment, so the difficulty does not arise.

$(A,V,\Lambda,\kappa_k,(x_i,q_i)_{i=1}^n)$ from

The prime-exclusion written as $(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0)$ omits only each particle's

derivations.claim: Under the Countable Choice assumption [A1], the Ewald supplier gives the reciprocal potential and energy formulas [F6]. Because the charges and assignment weights are real, $c_{-k}=c_k$, $\rho_{-k}=\overline{\rho_k}$, $a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}$, $D(-k)=\overline{D(k)}$, $b_{-k}=\overline{b_k}$, and $z_{-k}=\overline{z_k}$. Thus the sums over symmetric $\mathcal K$ are real and their displayed real-part forms agree with the reciprocal potentials. By [F3], $|\rho_k|\le Q$, $|z_k-\rho_k|\le QA_k$, and $|z_k|\le Q(1+A_k)$. Since $e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}=\overline{a_k(t)}$, [F6] gives the exact reciprocal potential. For each mode, $|z_k\overline{b_k}-\rho_k\overline{a_k}|\le |z_k-\rho_k||a_k|+|z_k||b_k-a_k|\le QA_k+Q(1+A_k)A_k=QA_k(2+A_k)$ using $|a_k|=1$. Sum with $c_k>0$ to obtain the potential bound.

The identity $\bigl||z_k|^2-|\rho_k|^2\bigr|\le |z_k-\rho_k|(|z_k|+|\rho_k|)$ and [F3] give $\bigl||z_k|^2-|\rho_k|^2\bigr|\le QA_k\bigl(Q(1+A_k)+Q\bigr)=Q^2A_k(2+A_k)$. Multiplying by $c_k/2$ and summing proves the energy bound.

The mode sums are finite. For $P\ge3$, and for $P=2$ off the assignment knots, [F4] supplies the classical derivatives. Since $z_k=\sum_jq_jb_k(t_j)$ by [F3], [F7] gives $

abla_xa_k(t_i))$, so the negative derivative is exactly $F_{\mathcal K,i}$. At a $P=2$ knot the chosen derivative is a procedure value, not a classical derivative.

Expanding $|z_k|^2$ with $z_k=\sum_jq_jb_k(t_j)$ shows that subtracting $C_M$ replaces the diagonal terms $q_i^2|b_k(t_i)|^2$ by $q_i^2$. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. For $\alpha>0$, define
$$g_\alpha(x)=\frac{\alpha^3}{\pi^{3/2}}e^{-\alpha^2|x|^2},\quad \operatorname{erf}(s)=\frac2{\sqrt\pi}\int_0^s e^{-t^2}\,dt,\quad \operatorname{erfc}(s)=1-\operatorname{erf}(s).$$
Here $\Delta=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}^2$, $\delta_0$ is the distribution
$\langle\delta_0,\varphi\rangle=\varphi(0)$, and a test function is a smooth
compactly supported function $\varphi$.
For $r=|x|>0$ put $\phi_\ell(r)=\operatorname{erf}(\alpha r)/r$ and
$\phi_s(r)=\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha r)/r$. Then $\phi_\ell$ extends
continuously to $r=0$, $-\Delta\phi_\ell=4\pi g_\alpha$ distributionally on
$\mathbb R^3$, and $-\Delta\phi_s=4\pi\delta_0-4\pi g_\alpha$. Moreover,
for every $s\ge0$,
$$\operatorname{erfc}(s)=\frac2{\sqrt\pi}\int_s^\infty e^{-t^2}\,dt,$$
$$\phi_s(r)=\frac1r-\frac{2\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}+O(r^2)\quad(r\downarrow0),$$
and for every $r>0$,
$$0\le\phi_s(r)\le\frac{e^{-\alpha^2r^2}}{\sqrt\pi\alpha r^2},\qquad |\phi_s'(r)|\le\frac{2\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\frac{e^{-\alpha^2r^2}}r+ \frac{e^{-\alpha^2r^2}}{\sqrt\pi\alpha r^3}.$$

Assume Countable Choice. For an invertible real $3\times3$ matrix $B$, put
$\Gamma=B\mathbb Z^3$ and
$$C_B=\bigl(2\|B^{-1}\|_2(1+\sqrt3\|B\|_2)+1\bigr)^3.$$
Here $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Euclidean operator norm. Uniformly over every
translate $y+\Gamma$ and every integer shell $m\ge0$,
$$\#\{z\in y+\Gamma:m\le|z|<m+1\}\le C_B(m+1)^3.$$

For $\beta>0$, any integer $p\ge0$, and integer $M\ge0$, set
$$T_p(\beta,M)=\sum_{m=M}^{\infty}(m+1)^p e^{-\beta m^2}.$$
For any integer $J\ge M$ satisfying $2\beta J(J+1)\ge p$, define
$$I_0(J,\beta)=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2\sqrt\beta}\operatorname{erfc}(\sqrt\beta J),\quad I_1(J,\beta)=\frac{e^{-\beta J^2}}{2\beta},$$
and recursively for $2\le s\le p$,
$$I_s(J,\beta)=\frac{J^{s-1}e^{-\beta J^2}}{2\beta} +\frac{s-1}{2\beta}I_{s-2}(J,\beta).$$
Then the finite controller
$$U_p(\beta,M,J)=\sum_{m=M}^{J}(m+1)^p e^{-\beta m^2} +\sum_{s=0}^{p}\binom ps I_s(J,\beta)$$
satisfies $T_p(\beta,M)\le U_p(\beta,M,J)$. Such a $J$ exists for every
$\beta>0$, $M\ge0$, and integer $p\ge0$.

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite point-source data
$(A,V,\Lambda,\kappa_k,(x_i,q_i)_{i=1}^n)$ from
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]], with pairwise distinct
source positions in $\mathbb T_A$. For $\alpha>0$ put
$$\sigma_k=\sum_iq_i e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i},\qquad c_k(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi}{V|\kappa_k|^2}e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}\quad(k\ne0).$$
For every off-source point $x\notin\bigcup_i(x_i+\Lambda)$, the absolutely
convergent Ewald potential
$$U_\alpha(x)=\sum_iq_i\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda} \frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha|x-x_i+\lambda|)}{|x-x_i+\lambda|} +\frac{4\pi}{V}\sum_{k\ne0}\frac{e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}}{|\kappa_k|^2} \sigma_k e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}$$
is the off-source representative of the unique mean-zero periodic solution of
$-\Delta u=4\pi\rho$. Hence it is independent of $\alpha$.

Define the regular part at $x_i$ by
$$\operatorname{FP}_{x_i}U_\alpha= \lim_{x\to x_i}\left(U_\alpha(x)-\frac{q_i}{|x-x_i|}\right).$$
The limit exists, is independent of $\alpha$, and the renormalized energy is
$$E=\frac12\sum_iq_i\operatorname{FP}_{x_i}U_\alpha =\frac12\sum_i\sum_{(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0)}q_iq_j \frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha|x_i-x_j+\lambda|)} {|x_i-x_j+\lambda|} +\frac12\sum_{k\ne0}c_k(\alpha)|\sigma_k|^2 -\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\sum_iq_i^2.$$
The prime-exclusion written as $(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0)$ omits only each particle's
own zero-image singularity.

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite point-source data
$(A,V,\Lambda,\kappa_k,(x_i,q_i)_{i=1}^n)$ from
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]], with pairwise distinct
source positions in $\mathbb T_A$. For $\alpha>0$ put

The prime-exclusion written as $(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0)$ omits only each particle's

Let $a<b$ be reals and let $f_k:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuously
differentiable: each $f_k$ is differentiable on $[a,b]$ and each derivative
$f_k'$ is continuous there ([[def-continuity-real]]). Suppose there is
$c\in[a,b]$ such that the real
sequence $(f_k(c))$ converges to $A$, and suppose $f_k'\to g$ uniformly on
$[a,b]$. Then there is a differentiable function $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ such
that

$$f_k\longrightarrow f\ \text{ uniformly},\qquad f'=g.$$

Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g[A] \subseteq B$ and let $f : B \to \mathbb{R}$, so that the composite
$f \circ g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined. Let $c \in A$ be a limit point of
$A$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]) at which $g$ is differentiable
([[def-derivative]]), put $b := g(c)$, and suppose $b$ is a limit point of $B$
at which $f$ is differentiable. Then $f \circ g$ is differentiable at $c$ and

$$(f \circ g)'(c) \;=\; f'\bigl(g(c)\bigr)\,g'(c) .$$

**Both limit-point hypotheses are needed, and neither is automatic.** That $c$
is a limit point of $A$ is what makes $g'(c)$ and $(f \circ g)'(c)$ defined
symbols; that $b = g(c)$ is a limit point of $B$ is what makes $f'(b)$ one.
Nothing forces the second: $g$ may be differentiable at $c$ and send $c$ to an
isolated point of $B$, and there $f'(b)$ is not defined and the formula asserts
nothing.

**No case analysis appears anywhere.** The naive difference-quotient proof
writes $\frac{f(g(x)) - f(g(c))}{g(x) - g(c)} \cdot \frac{g(x) - g(c)}{x - c}$
and then has to say what happens where $g(x) = g(c)$, which may occur at points
arbitrarily close to $c$. Carathéodory's factorisation never divides by the
inner increment, so the difficulty does not arise.

The functions $\sin$ and $\cos$ are differentiable on $\mathbb R$, with
$$(\sin x)'=\cos x,\qquad(\cos x)'=-\sin x.$$
Also $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$.

Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space and let $f_k:X\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous for
every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, where $\mathbb{R}$ has its usual metric
$d_{\mathbb{R}}(s,t)=|s-t|$. If $f_k\to f$ uniformly on $X$, then
$f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuous.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$. Suppose every partial derivative $\partial_jf$ exists on a neighbourhood of $a\in U$ and is continuous at $a$. Then $f$ is totally differentiable at $a$, and $Df(a)$ is the linear map with matrix $Jf(a)$.

derivations.claim: Fix a collision-free configuration and choose a small closed product of coordinate balls around its source positions, using local torus lifts, that remains collision-free. Finitely many nearby nonself images then stay a positive distance from the singularity. For large real-space shell index $m$, [F1] bounds the kernel by a constant times $e^{-\alpha^2m^2}$ and its first position derivatives by $(2\alpha+\alpha^{-1})e^{-\alpha^2m^2}/\sqrt\pi$. [F2] bounds the shell count uniformly over every translate; since the source-difference vectors stay in a bounded set, $|\lambda|\to\infty$ forces the corresponding distance to infinity uniformly. Thus the real energy series and each first-derivative series converge uniformly on this product. Finite partial sums are continuously differentiable and their values converge at one point by [F4]. Under [A1], apply [F5] along each real coordinate line to justify termwise differentiation of the real energy.

For the reciprocal energy, [F3] gives $|\sigma_k|\le Q$ and Gaussian decay of $c_k$, while [F6] gives $|\nabla_{x_i}\sigma_k|=|q_i||\kappa_k|$. The derivative of each summand $\frac12c_k|\sigma_k|^2$ is bounded by $c_kQ|q_i||\kappa_k|$. All nonzero modes in shells $m\ge1$ therefore have a summable position-uniform majorant $C(m+1)^3e^{-m^2/(4\alpha^2)}$ by [F2]; the remaining bounded ball contains finitely many modes because the reciprocal lattice is full rank. The energy summands themselves are bounded by $Q^2c_k/2$, whose shell sum also converges by [F2]–[F3]. Thus the reciprocal energy and all its first-derivative series converge uniformly on the same product. Finite partial sums have values converging at one point by [F4], so [F5] gives their termwise derivatives along every coordinate line.

Under Countable Choice [A1], use the Ewald representation [F4]. For $r>R$, the shell index $m$ is at least $M_R\ge1$. By [F1], each omitted real potential term is at most $e^{-\alpha^2m^2}/(\sqrt\pi\alpha m^2)$. The shell count [F2] and $m^{-2}\le1$ bound the total image tail for one source by $C_R(\sqrt\pi\alpha)^{-1}T_3(\alpha^2,M_R)$. Summing $|q_i|$ gives $B_R^U$.

For a reciprocal mode in the omitted shell $m\le|\kappa_k|<m+1$, with $m\ge M_K\ge1$, [F3] gives the potential summand bound $(4\pi Q/V)e^{-m^2/(4\alpha^2)}/m^2$. Multiply by [F2], use $m^{-2}\le1$, and sum to obtain $B_K^U$. The energy summand is one half the coefficient times $|\sigma_k|^2\le Q^2$, so the same count yields $B_K^E$.

Each coordinate derivative obtained in steps 1.1–1.2 is a locally uniform limit of continuous finite-sum derivatives, hence is continuous by [F7]. The open collision-free configuration set is a finite-dimensional Euclidean open set in local lifts. Applying the continuous-partials clause of [F7] shows the Ewald energy is totally differentiable there, with the termwise derivatives computed below as its gradient.

In a finite real-space partial sum truncated by the symmetric condition $|\lambda|\le L$, differentiating terms with $x_i$ in the first position gives one half of $q_i\sum_{j,\lambda}'q_j
abla\phi_s(|x_i-x_j+\lambda|)$. Terms with $x_i$ in the second position give $- rac12q_i\sum_{j,\lambda}'q_j
abla\phi_s(|x_j-x_i+\lambda|)$. By [F6] and the chain rule, $
abla\phi_s(|y|)=\phi_s'(|y|)y/|y|$ for $y
e0$, so this radial vector gradient is odd. Reindexing the second sum by $\lambda\mapsto-\lambda$ preserves the finite truncation and the excluded self term, and makes it equal to the first half. Passing to the limit is justified by step 1.1, so the full real energy gradient is $q_i\sum_{j,\lambda}'q_j\phi_s'(r_{ij\lambda})(x_i-x_j+\lambda)/r_{ij\lambda}$.

The real energy has the factor $1/2$ and charge-pair absolute sum at most $Q^2$, so the same shell estimate as in step 1.3 gives $B_R^E$. The radial derivative bound [F1] and $r\ge m\ge1$ imply $|\phi_s'(r)|\le(2\alpha+\alpha^{-1})e^{-\alpha^2m^2}/\sqrt\pi$. The real force formula proved in step 2.2, the shell count [F2], and $|q_i|\sum_j|q_j|=|q_i|Q$ give exactly $B_R^{F,i}$.

By the reciprocal force formula in step 3.1, each omitted reciprocal force mode has magnitude at most $(4\pi|q_i|Q/V)e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}/|\kappa_k|$, using $|\nabla_xa_k|=|\kappa_k|$ from [F6]. Since $|\kappa_k|\ge m\ge1$, this is at most $(4\pi|q_i|Q/V)e^{-m^2/(4\alpha^2)}$. The shell count [F2] and sum over $m\ge M_K$ give $B_K^{F,i}$.

The shell bounds are uniform in every translate, so no source-position dependence was introduced. Replacing $T_3$ by its finite upper controller preserves each inequality. Adding the real and reciprocal omitted terms by the triangle inequality gives the total Ewald cutoff error for potential, energy, and force.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $A\in GL_3(\mathbb R)$, let $\Lambda=A\mathbb Z^3$, let
$V=|\det A|$, and let $\mathbb T_A=\mathbb R^3/\Lambda$. These are the
full-rank lattice and covolume conventions of
[[def-full-rank-lattice-covolume-and-dual-lattice]]. The reciprocal lattice is
$\Lambda^*=A^{-T}\mathbb Z^3$. For $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ write
$$\kappa_k=2\pi A^{-T}k,\qquad e_k(x)=e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}.$$
Thus $e_k$ is a character of $\mathbb T_A$; the ordinary Fourier frequency is
$A^{-T}k$, while $\kappa_k$ is the angular physical frequency.

A finite point-source configuration consists of an integer $n\ge0$, points
$x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb T_A$ that are pairwise distinct when $n>1$, and
real charges $q_1,\ldots,q_n$. It is **neutral** when
$\sum_{i=1}^n q_i=0$. For a smooth periodic test function $\varphi$, the
point-source distribution is the linear functional
$$\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^nq_i\varphi(x_i).$$
Here smooth means that the periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$ has continuous
derivatives of every order, and the test-function topology is generated by the
seminorms $\max_{x\in A[0,1]^3}|\partial^\beta\varphi(x)|$ over all derivative
multi-indices $\beta$. A periodic distribution is a continuous complex-linear
functional for this topology. Its distributional Laplacian is defined by
$\langle-\Delta u,\varphi\rangle=\langle u,-\Delta\varphi\rangle$.

For a smooth periodic $\varphi$, its Fourier coefficient is
$$\widehat\varphi(k)=\frac1V\int_{A(0,1]^3}\varphi(x)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\,dx.$$
The source coefficient is
$$\widehat\rho(k)=\frac1V\sum_{i=1}^nq_i e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i};$$
in particular, neutral data have $\widehat\rho(0)=0$. For a periodic
distribution $u$, define $\widehat u(k)=V^{-1}\langle u,e_{-k}\rangle$. The
**mean-zero periodic Poisson solution** is a periodic distribution $u$ satisfying
$-\Delta u=4\pi\rho$ and $\widehat u(0)=0$. This definition fixes the
zero-mode convention; no nonneutral periodic solution is implicit.

The Coulomb energy convention is the half-sum of each source charge times the
regular part of its potential, after subtracting its own singular term
$q_i/|x-x_i|$. The resulting finite part is called the **renormalized
self-energy convention**. Its Ewald formula is established in this development.

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite point-source data
$(A,V,\Lambda,\kappa_k,(x_i,q_i)_{i=1}^n)$ from
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]], with pairwise distinct
source positions in $\mathbb T_A$. For $\alpha>0$ put
$$\sigma_k=\sum_iq_i e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i},\qquad c_k(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi}{V|\kappa_k|^2}e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}\quad(k\ne0).$$
For every off-source point $x\notin\bigcup_i(x_i+\Lambda)$, the absolutely
convergent Ewald potential
$$U_\alpha(x)=\sum_iq_i\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda} \frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha|x-x_i+\lambda|)}{|x-x_i+\lambda|} +\frac{4\pi}{V}\sum_{k\ne0}\frac{e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}}{|\kappa_k|^2} \sigma_k e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}$$
is the off-source representative of the unique mean-zero periodic solution of
$-\Delta u=4\pi\rho$. Hence it is independent of $\alpha$.

Define the regular part at $x_i$ by
$$\operatorname{FP}_{x_i}U_\alpha= \lim_{x\to x_i}\left(U_\alpha(x)-\frac{q_i}{|x-x_i|}\right).$$
The limit exists, is independent of $\alpha$, and the renormalized energy is
$$E=\frac12\sum_iq_i\operatorname{FP}_{x_i}U_\alpha =\frac12\sum_i\sum_{(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0)}q_iq_j \frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha|x_i-x_j+\lambda|)} {|x_i-x_j+\lambda|} +\frac12\sum_{k\ne0}c_k(\alpha)|\sigma_k|^2 -\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\sum_iq_i^2.$$
The prime-exclusion written as $(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0)$ omits only each particle's
own zero-image singularity.

Assume Countable Choice and the neutral finite configuration and full-rank cell of
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Fix $\alpha>0$. Let
$Q=\sum_i|q_i|$, choose real and reciprocal cutoffs $R,K\ge1$, and put
$M_R=\lfloor R\rfloor$, $M_K=\lfloor K\rfloor$. Let $C_R=C_A$ be the shell
constant for $\Lambda=A\mathbb Z^3$ and $C_K=C_{2\pi A^{-T}}$ the shell constant
for the angular reciprocal lattice. For the real-space cutoff, retain all
$(i,j,\lambda)$ with $|x_i-x_j+\lambda|\le R$ except $(i,i,0)$. For the
reciprocal cutoff, retain all $k\ne0$ with $|\kappa_k|\le K$. Use the
$T_3(\beta,M)$ controller of
[[lem-ewald-lattice-shell-gaussian-tail-controllers]]. Then the omitted tails
in the exact Ewald potential, energy, and particle force satisfy
$$B_R^U=\frac{QC_R}{\sqrt\pi\alpha}T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),\qquad B_R^E=\frac{Q^2C_R}{2\sqrt\pi\alpha}T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),$$
$$B_R^{F,i}=\frac{|q_i|QC_R}{\sqrt\pi}(2\alpha+\alpha^{-1}) T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),$$
and
$$B_K^U=\frac{4\pi QC_K}{V}T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K),\qquad B_K^E=\frac{2\pi Q^2C_K}{V}T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K),$$
$$B_K^{F,i}=\frac{4\pi|q_i|QC_K}{V} T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K).$$
For a certified finite value, replace each $T_3$ by the corresponding finite
upper controller $U_3$. The real force is evaluated only away from collisions;
no field bound is asserted at a point source.

The exact force is the negative gradient of the renormalized energy. With
$r_{ij\lambda}=|x_i-x_j+\lambda|$ and $a_k(t_i)=e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i}$,
it is
$$F_i=-q_i\sum_{j=1}^n\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}'q_j\phi_s'(r_{ij\lambda})\frac{x_i-x_j+\lambda}{r_{ij\lambda}}-q_i\sum_{k\ne0}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\sigma_k}\nabla_xa_k(t_i)).$$
The prime excludes only $(j,\lambda)=(i,0)$; the absolutely convergent
reciprocal sum is real by pairing $k$ and $-k$.

Assume Countable Choice and the neutral finite configuration and full-rank cell of
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Fix $\alpha>0$. Let
$Q=\sum_i|q_i|$, choose real and reciprocal cutoffs $R,K\ge1$, and put
$M_R=\lfloor R\rfloor$, $M_K=\lfloor K\rfloor$. Let $C_R=C_A$ be the shell
constant for $\Lambda=A\mathbb Z^3$ and $C_K=C_{2\pi A^{-T}}$ the shell constant
for the angular reciprocal lattice. For the real-space cutoff, retain all
$(i,j,\lambda)$ with $|x_i-x_j+\lambda|\le R$ except $(i,i,0)$. For the
reciprocal cutoff, retain all $k\ne0$ with $|\kappa_k|\le K$. Use the
$T_3(\beta,M)$ controller of
[[lem-ewald-lattice-shell-gaussian-tail-controllers]]. Then the omitted tails
in the exact Ewald potential, energy, and particle force satisfy
$$B_R^U=\frac{QC_R}{\sqrt\pi\alpha}T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),\qquad B_R^E=\frac{Q^2C_R}{2\sqrt\pi\alpha}T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),$$
$$B_R^{F,i}=\frac{|q_i|QC_R}{\sqrt\pi}(2\alpha+\alpha^{-1}) T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),$$
and
$$B_K^U=\frac{4\pi QC_K}{V}T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K),\qquad B_K^E=\frac{2\pi Q^2C_K}{V}T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K),$$
$$B_K^{F,i}=\frac{4\pi|q_i|QC_K}{V} T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K).$$
For a certified finite value, replace each $T_3$ by the corresponding finite
upper controller $U_3$. The real force is evaluated only away from collisions;
no field bound is asserted at a point source.

The exact force is the negative gradient of the renormalized energy. With
$r_{ij\lambda}=|x_i-x_j+\lambda|$ and $a_k(t_i)=e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i}$,
it is
$$F_i=-q_i\sum_{j=1}^n\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}'q_j\phi_s'(r_{ij\lambda})\frac{x_i-x_j+\lambda}{r_{ij\lambda}}-q_i\sum_{k\ne0}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\sigma_k}\nabla_xa_k(t_i)).$$
The prime excludes only $(j,\lambda)=(i,0)$; the absolutely convergent
reciprocal sum is real by pairing $k$ and $-k$.

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite source data on the cell $A\mathbb Z^3$
from [[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Fix $\alpha>0$,
integers $M_r\ge1$, an order $P\ge2$, and a finite symmetric set
$\mathcal K\subset\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$ whose signed representatives are
injective modulo $(M_1,M_2,M_3)$ and satisfy $|k_r|<M_r/2$. Require $D(k)\ne0$
for every $k\in\mathcal K$, and let $c_k=4\pi e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}/(V|\kappa_k|^2)$ be the positive Ewald coefficient. Use the assignment factors $a_k,b_k,\rho_k,z_k$ of [[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]], and put $Q=\sum_j|q_j|$.

For a query point $x$ write $t=A^{-1}x$ modulo $\mathbb Z^3$ and define the retained exact and mesh reciprocal potentials by
$$U_{\mathcal K}(x)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\rho_k\overline{a_k(t)}),\qquad U_{M,\mathcal K}(x)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(z_k\overline{b_k(t)}).$$
Define $E_{\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|\rho_k|^2$ and $E_{M,\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|z_k|^2$. For each mode let $A_k$ be the source-alias controller in [[lem-ewald-pme-spline-alias-and-dft-normalization]], and let $B_k$ be the derivative-alias controller in [[lem-ewald-pme-derivative-window-alias-bound]].

Let a complex-vector derivative/gather value $d_k(t)$ satisfy $\|d_k(t)-\mathfrak d_k(t)\|_2\le H_k$ for a stated $H_k\ge0$, where $\mathfrak d_k$ is the declared derivative branch of [[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]] and $\nabla_x=A^{-T}\nabla_t$. The uncorrected mesh and exact reciprocal forces are
$$F^d_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{z_k}d_k(t_i)),\qquad F_{\mathcal K,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\rho_k}\nabla_xa_k(t_i)).$$
Then for every query point $x$,
$$|U_{M,\mathcal K}(x)-U_{\mathcal K}(x)|\le Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k),\qquad |E_{M,\mathcal K}-E_{\mathcal K}|\le\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k),$$
and for every particle $i$,
$$\|F^d_{M,i}-F_{\mathcal K,i}\|_2\le |q_i|Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\bigl[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k+(1+A_k)H_k\bigr].$$

For the declared energy-gradient gather $d_k=\mathfrak d_k$ (so $H_k=0$), the mesh force is $-\nabla_{x_i}E_{M,\mathcal K}$ wherever the classical derivative exists. This holds everywhere for $P\ge3$ and off the assignment knots for $P=2$; at a $P=2$ knot the selected one-sided derivative or its average is a procedure value, with the same bound but without a differentiability claim.

The optional diagonal self correction is
$$C_M=\frac12\sum_iq_i^2\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k(|b_k(t_i)|^2-1),\qquad E^{\rm corr}_{M,\mathcal K}=E_{M,\mathcal K}-C_M.$$
For its finite cyclic implementation, set $h_k=c_k/|D(k)|^2$ on $\mathcal K$,
$$\gamma_d=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}h_ke^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_rd_r/M_r},\qquad S_i=\sum_{\ell,m\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t_i)w_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}.$$
Then $\gamma$ is real and even, $S_i=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|b_k(t_i)|^2$, and, on every differentiable branch (or as the same declared one-sided branch at a $P=2$ knot),
$$\nabla_{x_i}(S_i/2)=\sum_{\ell,m\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t_i)\nabla_xw_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}.$$
Consequently this local cyclic-kernel expression computes $C_M$ and its derivative exactly in real arithmetic.
The finite tensor-transform gathers also have the exact real-arithmetic forms
$$U_{M,\mathcal K}(x)=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t_x)u_\ell,\qquad u_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\frac{c_kz_k}{D(k)}e^{2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r},$$
$$F_{M,i}=-q_i\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}\lambda_\ell\nabla_xw_\ell(t_i),\qquad \lambda_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\frac{c_k\overline{z_k}}{\overline{D(k)}}e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}.$$
These identities hold with the declared derivative branch, including the selected one-sided $P=2$ knot value.
It satisfies
$$|E^{\rm corr}_{M,\mathcal K}-E_{\mathcal K}|\le\frac{Q^2-\sum_iq_i^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k).$$
In the energy-gradient branch its exactly differentiated force is
$$F^{\rm corr}_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\overline{z_k-q_ib_k(t_i)}\,\mathfrak d_k(t_i)\bigr),$$
and
$$\|F^{\rm corr}_{M,i}-F_{\mathcal K,i}\|_2\le |q_i|(Q-|q_i|)\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\bigl[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k\bigr].$$
The corrected force is the negative classical energy gradient in the same differentiable cases; at a $P=2$ knot it is only the declared branch value. No pointwise error estimate here replaces an RMS estimate, and no claim is made that a different spectral differentiation rule is the gradient of the mesh energy.

Let $n\ge1$. A **full-rank lattice** in $\mathbb R^n$ is a subgroup
$\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ of the form

$$\Lambda=A\mathbb Z^n=\Bigl\{\sum_{i=1}^n k_ia_i:k=(k_1,\dots,k_n)\in\mathbb Z^n\Bigr\},$$

where $A$ is an invertible real $n\times n$ matrix with columns $a_1,\dots,a_n$;
here $Ak$ is the matrix product ([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]) and
the column matrix $Ak$ is identified with the vector it represents. A
full-rank lattice is exactly a full Euclidean lattice in the sense of
[[def-full-euclidean-lattice-and-covolume]]: invertibility of $A$ makes its
columns linearly independent over $\mathbb R$
([[thm-real-square-matrix-invertible-iff-determinant-nonzero]]), so they form a
real basis of $\mathbb R^n$ and $\Lambda$ is their $\mathbb Z$-span, and
conversely the basis matrix of every full Euclidean lattice is invertible. The
**covolume** of $\Lambda$ is

$$\operatorname{covol}(\Lambda):=|\det A|>0,$$

with the determinant and the real absolute value of
[[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]], and the **dual lattice** is

$$\Lambda^*:=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^n:\xi\cdot\lambda\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every }\lambda\in\Lambda\}=A^{-T}\mathbb Z^n,$$

where $\xi\cdot\lambda$ is the Euclidean inner product
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), $A^{-T}:=(A^{-1})^{T}=(A^{T})^{-1}$ is formed
with the transpose of [[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]] and the inverse of
[[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]
([[prop-transpose-laws]] for the identity $(A^{-1})^{T}=(A^{T})^{-1}$, and
[[thm-real-square-matrix-invertible-iff-determinant-nonzero]] for the existence
of $A^{-1}$).

**Well-definedness: the presentation does not matter.** Suppose
$B\mathbb Z^n=A\mathbb Z^n$ for a second invertible real matrix $B$. Then
$U:=A^{-1}B$ has integer entries: each column $b_j$ of $B$ lies in
$A\mathbb Z^n$, say $b_j=Au_j$ with $u_j\in\mathbb Z^n$, so
$U=(u_1\ \cdots\ u_n)\in M_n(\mathbb Z)$
([[def-matrices-over-a-commutative-ring]],
[[def-ring-matrix-product-identity-and-transpose]]). Exchanging the roles of
$A$ and $B$ shows likewise that $U^{-1}=B^{-1}A$ has integer entries. Hence
$\det U\in\mathbb Z$ and $\det U^{-1}\in\mathbb Z$, and
$\det U\cdot\det U^{-1}=\det(UU^{-1})=\det I_n=1$
([[thm-determinant-multiplicative]], [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]);
by [[lem-units-of-z]] the only way two integers can multiply to $1$ is
$\det U=\det U^{-1}=\pm1$ (with the same sign). Consequently
$|\det B|=|\det A|\,|\det U|=|\det A|$, so the covolume is independent of the
presentation. For the dual, $B^{-T}\mathbb Z^n=A^{-T}U^{-T}\mathbb Z^n$ by
[[prop-transpose-laws]], and $U^{-T}=(U^{-1})^{T}$ as well as $U^{T}$ have
integer entries ([[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]]); matrices with integer entries
send $\mathbb Z^n$ into $\mathbb Z^n$ under matrix multiplication
([[def-ring-matrix-product-identity-and-transpose]]), so
$U^{-T}\mathbb Z^n\subseteq\mathbb Z^n$ and, applying the same statement to the
integer matrix $U^{T}=(U^{-T})^{-1}$, also
$\mathbb Z^n\subseteq U^{-T}\mathbb Z^n$. Hence $U^{-T}\mathbb Z^n=\mathbb Z^n$
and $B^{-T}\mathbb Z^n=A^{-T}\mathbb Z^n$.

**The dual in closed form.** For $\xi=A^{-T}m$ with $m\in\mathbb Z^n$ and
$\lambda=Ak$ with $k\in\mathbb Z^n$ one has
$\xi\cdot\lambda=(A^{-T}m)\cdot(Ak)=m\cdot k\in\mathbb Z$, because
$(A^{-T}m)\cdot(Ak)=m\cdot(A^{-1}Ak)$; so $A^{-T}\mathbb Z^n$ is contained in
the defining set. Conversely, if $\xi\cdot\lambda\in\mathbb Z$ for every
$\lambda\in\Lambda$, then testing $\lambda=a_j=Ae_j$ gives
$\xi\cdot a_j=(A^{T}\xi)_j\in\mathbb Z$ for every $j$, so
$A^{T}\xi\in\mathbb Z^n$ and $\xi=A^{-T}(A^{T}\xi)\in A^{-T}\mathbb Z^n$. This
also shows that the second description of $\Lambda^*$ depends only on
$\Lambda$. The dual is itself a full-rank lattice: $A^{-T}$ is invertible, its
columns being a real basis, and
$\operatorname{covol}(\Lambda^*)=|\det A^{-T}|=|\det A^{-1}|=|\det A|^{-1}=\operatorname{covol}(\Lambda)^{-1}$,
using $\det A^{-T}=\det A^{-1}$ ([[thm-determinant-of-transpose]]) and
$\det A^{-1}=(\det A)^{-1}$ ([[cor-determinant-of-an-inverse]]). For
$\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n$, that is $A=I_n$, one gets $\Lambda^*=\mathbb Z^n$
because $I_n^{-T}=I_n$ ([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]).

**Characters.** For $\lambda^*\in\mathbb R^n$ put
$\chi_{\lambda^*}(x):=e^{2\pi i\,\lambda^*\cdot x}$, with the complex
exponential of [[def-complex-exponential]]. Then
$\chi_{\lambda^*}(x+\lambda)=\chi_{\lambda^*}(x)e^{2\pi i\,\lambda^*\cdot\lambda}$
for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, so $\chi_{\lambda^*}$ is $\Lambda$-periodic
exactly when $e^{2\pi i\,\lambda^*\cdot\lambda}=1$ for every
$\lambda\in\Lambda$, that is ([[thm-kernel-and-fibres-of-complex-exponential]])
exactly when $\lambda^*\cdot\lambda\in\mathbb Z$ for every
$\lambda\in\Lambda$ --- precisely the condition $\lambda^*\in\Lambda^*$. Thus
$\lambda^*\mapsto\chi_{\lambda^*}$ is a bijection from $\Lambda^*$ onto the set
of exponential characters $\chi_{\lambda^*}$ of the torus
$\mathbb R^n/\Lambda$, and it is a group isomorphism for pointwise
multiplication because $\chi_{\lambda^*+\eta^*}=\chi_{\lambda^*}\chi_{\eta^*}$;
this is the lattice case of the characters of
[[def-pontryagin-dual-and-compact-open-topology]]. The assertion is about the
characters of the displayed exponential form; no claim is made here that every
continuous character of $\mathbb R^n/\Lambda$ is of that form.

No choice principle is used anywhere in this item.

Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g[A] \subseteq B$ and let $f : B \to \mathbb{R}$, so that the composite
$f \circ g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined. Let $c \in A$ be a limit point of
$A$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]) at which $g$ is differentiable
([[def-derivative]]), put $b := g(c)$, and suppose $b$ is a limit point of $B$
at which $f$ is differentiable. Then $f \circ g$ is differentiable at $c$ and

$$(f \circ g)'(c) \;=\; f'\bigl(g(c)\bigr)\,g'(c) .$$

**Both limit-point hypotheses are needed, and neither is automatic.** That $c$
is a limit point of $A$ is what makes $g'(c)$ and $(f \circ g)'(c)$ defined
symbols; that $b = g(c)$ is a limit point of $B$ is what makes $f'(b)$ one.
Nothing forces the second: $g$ may be differentiable at $c$ and send $c$ to an
isolated point of $B$, and there $f'(b)$ is not defined and the formula asserts
nothing.

**No case analysis appears anywhere.** The naive difference-quotient proof
writes $\frac{f(g(x)) - f(g(c))}{g(x) - g(c)} \cdot \frac{g(x) - g(c)}{x - c}$
and then has to say what happens where $g(x) = g(c)$, which may occur at points
arbitrarily close to $c$. Carathéodory's factorisation never divides by the
inner increment, so the difficulty does not arise.

The functions $\sin$ and $\cos$ are differentiable on $\mathbb R$, with
$$(\sin x)'=\cos x,\qquad(\cos x)'=-\sin x.$$
Also $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$.

Let $A\in GL_3(\mathbb R)$, let $\Lambda=A\mathbb Z^3$, let
$V=|\det A|$, and let $\mathbb T_A=\mathbb R^3/\Lambda$. These are the
full-rank lattice and covolume conventions of
[[def-full-rank-lattice-covolume-and-dual-lattice]]. The reciprocal lattice is
$\Lambda^*=A^{-T}\mathbb Z^3$. For $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ write
$$\kappa_k=2\pi A^{-T}k,\qquad e_k(x)=e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}.$$
Thus $e_k$ is a character of $\mathbb T_A$; the ordinary Fourier frequency is
$A^{-T}k$, while $\kappa_k$ is the angular physical frequency.

A finite point-source configuration consists of an integer $n\ge0$, points
$x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb T_A$ that are pairwise distinct when $n>1$, and
real charges $q_1,\ldots,q_n$. It is **neutral** when
$\sum_{i=1}^n q_i=0$. For a smooth periodic test function $\varphi$, the
point-source distribution is the linear functional
$$\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^nq_i\varphi(x_i).$$
Here smooth means that the periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$ has continuous
derivatives of every order, and the test-function topology is generated by the
seminorms $\max_{x\in A[0,1]^3}|\partial^\beta\varphi(x)|$ over all derivative
multi-indices $\beta$. A periodic distribution is a continuous complex-linear
functional for this topology. Its distributional Laplacian is defined by
$\langle-\Delta u,\varphi\rangle=\langle u,-\Delta\varphi\rangle$.

For a smooth periodic $\varphi$, its Fourier coefficient is
$$\widehat\varphi(k)=\frac1V\int_{A(0,1]^3}\varphi(x)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\,dx.$$
The source coefficient is
$$\widehat\rho(k)=\frac1V\sum_{i=1}^nq_i e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i};$$
in particular, neutral data have $\widehat\rho(0)=0$. For a periodic
distribution $u$, define $\widehat u(k)=V^{-1}\langle u,e_{-k}\rangle$. The
**mean-zero periodic Poisson solution** is a periodic distribution $u$ satisfying
$-\Delta u=4\pi\rho$ and $\widehat u(0)=0$. This definition fixes the
zero-mode convention; no nonneutral periodic solution is implicit.

The Coulomb energy convention is the half-sum of each source charge times the
regular part of its potential, after subtracting its own singular term
$q_i/|x-x_i|$. The resulting finite part is called the **renormalized
self-energy convention**. Its Ewald formula is established in this development.

Fix an instance of the operationwise floating-point model in [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], with representable real set $\mathbb F$. Input $N\ge1$, $x\in\mathbb C^N$ whose real and imaginary coordinates all belong to $\mathbb F$, an exact rational phase tolerance $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer dyadic exponent limits $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$, an initial phase precision $p_0\ge2$, a finite precision cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, a finite elementary-series cap $J\ge1$, and a maximum radix-two recursion depth $d_{\max}\ge0$. At precision $p$, phase endpoints use the dyadic format with precision $p$ and exponent limits $e_{\min},e_{\max}$. Before any certified phase is used as an arithmetic operand or stored in an input vector to a computed subroutine, require its real and imaginary coordinates to belong to $\mathbb F$; otherwise return `range-failure` with that phase index before the operation or subcall. Use the same floating-point model instance throughout all recursive calls. The output convention is the **unnormalised** DFT $X_k=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}x_je^{-2\pi ijk/N}$ ([[def-unnormalised-engineering-dft-and-conversion]]); the procedure returns an approximate vector or the first `inconclusive`/`range-failure` status.

1. For $N=1$, return $x_0$.
2. If $N=2^m$ with $m\ge1$, call [[alg-na-computed-unitary-radix-two-fft]] in `forward` mode with controls $(\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J,d_{\max})$ and multiply each output by the computed scalar $\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt N)$. A failed subcall or scale operation returns its status.
3. If $N$ is composite and not a power of two, find its least divisor $r$ with $1<r<N$ by trial division and put $s=N/r$. For $u=0,\ldots,r-1$, recursively call this procedure with the same controls on the strided vector $(x_{u+rv})_{v=0}^{s-1}$ to obtain an approximate unnormalised length-$s$ DFT $U_u$. For each $0\le k_2<s$ and $0\le u<r$, call [[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]] on $(q,\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J)$ with $q=-2uk_2/N$ to obtain the twiddle enclosure, then multiply its returned phase by $U_u(k_2)$ using $\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}$. For each $0\le k_2<s$, apply this procedure recursively, with the same controls, to the length-$r$ vector of these products indexed by $u$, and for every $0\le k_1<r$ store its output $k_1$ at index $k_2+sk_1$. Propagate any failed phase or arithmetic status.
4. If $N$ is prime, set $M$ to the least power of two with $M\ge2N-1$. For each $0\le j<N$, call [[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]] on $(q,\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J)$ with $q=-j^2/N$ to obtain $\widehat\alpha_j$, and set $a_j=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat\alpha_jx_j)$; set the remaining entries of $a\in\mathbb C^M$ to zero. For each $-(N-1)\le t\le N-1$, obtain $\widehat\beta_t$ by the same call with $q=t^2/N$ and set $b_{[t]_M}=\widehat\beta_t$, setting other entries of $b$ to zero. Compute the cyclic convolution with [[alg-na-computed-fft-cyclic-and-linear-convolution]] in `cyclic` mode using controls $(\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J,d_{\max})$. For each $0\le k<N$, obtain $\widehat\gamma_k$ by the same phase call with $q=-k^2/N$ and set $\widehat X_k=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat\gamma_k\widehat c_k)$. Return the first $N$ entries or the first failure status.

The divisor search and phase-enclosure work have separate integer/interval budgets and are not counted as complex arithmetic operations in the operation-count theorem. The exact factorization lemmas and the chirp-phase error theorem state what is guaranteed; this procedure by itself makes no general mixed-radix stability claim.

For this theorem, define the **formal exact-constant model** as the complete finite branch schedule of [[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]], with its radix-two subdivision cap sufficient to finish every call, every certified-phase output (including nested calls) replaced by its exact target $e^{\pi iq}$, and every arithmetic instruction interpreted exactly. Phase-evaluation and arithmetic-failure statuses are suppressed in this idealized model; it is not an exactness claim about the computed routine, whose phase values are enclosures. For every integer $N\ge1$ and $x\in\mathbb C^N$, the formal model returns the unnormalised DFT $X_k=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}x_je^{-2\pi ijk/N}$. Count complex additions, multiplications, and scalar operations at each butterfly, but exclude integer factor search, exact phase generation, interval evaluation, storage, and bit complexity. If $M$ is the least power of two at least $2N-1$ in a Bluestein prime branch, that branch costs $O(M\log M)$; for $N\ge2$, the full arbitrary-length recursion costs $O(N\log N)$, while $N=1$ takes constant work.

derivations.claim: From [F1], $\kappa_k=2\pi A^{-T}k$, so $|\kappa_k|\le K_c$ implies $|k|\le\|A^T\|_2K_c/(2\pi)$. Only finitely many integer vectors lie in that bounded ball by [F5]. Therefore $\mathcal B_{K_c}$ and $\mathcal M_{K_c}$ are finite, and all missing in-ball sums in the Statement are finite.

Choose $J_R,J_K$ as in the Statement. The finite Gaussian controllers $U_3$ bound the exact real and reciprocal shell tails by [F3], giving $\overline B_R^U,\overline B_R^E,\overline B_R^{F,i},\overline B_K^U,\overline B_K^E,\overline B_K^{F,i}$.

For each omitted in-ball mode $m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}$, $|\rho_m|\le Q$ and $|e^{i\kappa_m\cdot x}|=1$ give potential magnitude at most $c_mQ$. Its energy term is $\frac12c_m|\rho_m|^2\le\frac12c_mQ^2$. By [F7], differentiating its finite reciprocal energy term gives exact force $-q_ic_m\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\rho_m}\nabla_xa_m(t_i))$, whose magnitude is at most $|q_i|c_m|\rho_m||\kappa_m|\le|q_i|Qc_m|\kappa_m|$. Summing these inequalities over the finite omitted set accounts for every in-ball mode, including modes excluded by Nyquist restrictions.

The retained-mode mesh errors are bounded by [F4]. In the uncorrected energy branch this is $\frac12Q^2\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)$; in the corrected branch it is $\frac12(Q^2-\sum_iq_i^2)\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)$. The force contributions are the corresponding $|q_i|Q$ and $|q_i|(Q-|q_i|)$ sums in [F4], and the retained potential contribution is $Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)$.

The exact Ewald series is the sum of the full real-space term, all retained reciprocal modes, all in-ball omitted reciprocal modes, and the reciprocal tail beyond $K_c$, with the exact self constant in the energy. The finite approximations include the real terms through $R$, the selected mesh approximation on $\mathcal K$, and that same self constant. Thus their exact-real differences split into the real cutoff tail, the reciprocal shell tail, the finite omitted in-ball terms, and the retained mesh alias/differentiation error. Step 1.2 bounds the real and reciprocal cutoff tails, step 1.3 accounts for every omitted in-ball mode, and step 1.4 bounds the retained mesh error. By [F3], [F4], and the triangle inequality, the absolute values or norms of these parts sum to the first terms displayed in each $\eta$.

The arithmetic assumptions [F6] give $|\widehat U-\widetilde U|\le\varepsilon_U$, $|\widehat E^\chi-\widetilde E^\chi|\le\varepsilon_E$, and $\|\widehat F_i^\chi-\widetilde F_i^\chi\|_2\le\varepsilon_{F,i}$. Applying the triangle inequality to step 2.1 yields the three stated certificates. If an arithmetic radius is unavailable, the corresponding inequality has no supplied numerical right-hand side and no certificate is returned.

For fixed $P\ge2$, the finite support enclosure gives at most $P+2\le2P$ candidates per coordinate. Thus each particle's spread and potential/force gathers use $O(P^3)$ support tuples; grid initialization costs $O(N_g)$ and is absorbed by the transform count. A tensor transform along coordinate $r$ consists of $N_g/M_r$ one-dimensional transforms of length $M_r$. By [F8] this costs $O(N_g\log(2M_r))$, and summing over the three coordinates gives $O(N_g\log(2N_g))$. The uncorrected computation uses one forward transform and at most two inverse/gather transforms. The finite real-image and mode/controller loops contribute $\mathsf N_{\mathrm{img}}+\mathsf N_{\mathrm{cert}}$ by definition, proving the stated total count. The optional correction adds one transform to form its cyclic kernel and at most $(P+2)^6=O(P^6)$ support-pair products per particle, which gives its stated cost. The arithmetic radii are certified separately and do not follow from this operation count.

source positions in $\mathbb T_A$. For $\alpha>0$ put
$$\sigma_k=\sum_iq_i e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i},\qquad c_k(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi}{V|\kappa_k|^2}e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}\quad(k\ne0).$$

convergent Ewald potential
$$U_\alpha(x)=\sum_iq_i\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda} \frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha|x-x_i+\lambda|)}{|x-x_i+\lambda|} +\frac{4\pi}{V}\sum_{k\ne0}\frac{e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}}{|\kappa_k|^2} \sigma_k e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}$$

$$E=\frac12\sum_iq_i\operatorname{FP}_{x_i}U_\alpha =\frac12\sum_i\sum_{(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0)}q_iq_j \frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha|x_i-x_j+\lambda|)} {|x_i-x_j+\lambda|} +\frac12\sum_{k\ne0}c_k(\alpha)|\sigma_k|^2 -\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\sum_iq_i^2.$$

derivations.claim: The configuration is neutral, and its two torus positions are distinct. For $\lambda\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$, $|\lambda|\ge1$, while every image of $x_2$ relative to $x_1$ has first coordinate in $\mathbb Z+1/2$ and hence distance at least $1/2$. Thus for $0<r<1/4$, every real-space image except $(i,\lambda)=(1,0)$ stays at distance at least $1/4$ from $x$. By [F3], the finitely many nearby nonself terms and their first derivatives are uniformly bounded there, and the Gaussian shell bound makes the remaining potential and derivative tails uniformly convergent. The reciprocal series and its gradient are bounded by [F4]. Hence the nonself periodic remainder and its gradient are bounded near $x_1$.

Writing $r=|x-x_1|$, [F2] gives the self-potential expansion $\phi_s(r)=1/r-2\alpha/\sqrt\pi+O(r^2)$. Substituting the stated error-function expansion into the derivative formula in [F2] cancels the $r^{-1}$ terms and gives $\phi_s'(r)=-1/r^2+O(r)$. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice and the neutral finite configuration and full-rank cell of
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Fix $\alpha>0$. Let
$Q=\sum_i|q_i|$, choose real and reciprocal cutoffs $R,K\ge1$, and put
$M_R=\lfloor R\rfloor$, $M_K=\lfloor K\rfloor$. Let $C_R=C_A$ be the shell
constant for $\Lambda=A\mathbb Z^3$ and $C_K=C_{2\pi A^{-T}}$ the shell constant
for the angular reciprocal lattice. For the real-space cutoff, retain all
$(i,j,\lambda)$ with $|x_i-x_j+\lambda|\le R$ except $(i,i,0)$. For the
reciprocal cutoff, retain all $k\ne0$ with $|\kappa_k|\le K$. Use the
$T_3(\beta,M)$ controller of
[[lem-ewald-lattice-shell-gaussian-tail-controllers]]. Then the omitted tails
in the exact Ewald potential, energy, and particle force satisfy
$$B_R^U=\frac{QC_R}{\sqrt\pi\alpha}T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),\qquad B_R^E=\frac{Q^2C_R}{2\sqrt\pi\alpha}T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),$$
$$B_R^{F,i}=\frac{|q_i|QC_R}{\sqrt\pi}(2\alpha+\alpha^{-1}) T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),$$
and
$$B_K^U=\frac{4\pi QC_K}{V}T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K),\qquad B_K^E=\frac{2\pi Q^2C_K}{V}T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K),$$
$$B_K^{F,i}=\frac{4\pi|q_i|QC_K}{V} T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K).$$
For a certified finite value, replace each $T_3$ by the corresponding finite
upper controller $U_3$. The real force is evaluated only away from collisions;
no field bound is asserted at a point source.

The exact force is the negative gradient of the renormalized energy. With
$r_{ij\lambda}=|x_i-x_j+\lambda|$ and $a_k(t_i)=e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i}$,
it is
$$F_i=-q_i\sum_{j=1}^n\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}'q_j\phi_s'(r_{ij\lambda})\frac{x_i-x_j+\lambda}{r_{ij\lambda}}-q_i\sum_{k\ne0}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\sigma_k}\nabla_xa_k(t_i)).$$
The prime excludes only $(j,\lambda)=(i,0)$; the absolutely convergent
reciprocal sum is real by pairing $k$ and $-k$.

Assume Countable Choice. For an invertible real $3\times3$ matrix $B$, put
$\Gamma=B\mathbb Z^3$ and
$$C_B=\bigl(2\|B^{-1}\|_2(1+\sqrt3\|B\|_2)+1\bigr)^3.$$
Here $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Euclidean operator norm. Uniformly over every
translate $y+\Gamma$ and every integer shell $m\ge0$,
$$\#\{z\in y+\Gamma:m\le|z|<m+1\}\le C_B(m+1)^3.$$

For $\beta>0$, any integer $p\ge0$, and integer $M\ge0$, set
$$T_p(\beta,M)=\sum_{m=M}^{\infty}(m+1)^p e^{-\beta m^2}.$$
For any integer $J\ge M$ satisfying $2\beta J(J+1)\ge p$, define
$$I_0(J,\beta)=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2\sqrt\beta}\operatorname{erfc}(\sqrt\beta J),\quad I_1(J,\beta)=\frac{e^{-\beta J^2}}{2\beta},$$
and recursively for $2\le s\le p$,
$$I_s(J,\beta)=\frac{J^{s-1}e^{-\beta J^2}}{2\beta} +\frac{s-1}{2\beta}I_{s-2}(J,\beta).$$
Then the finite controller
$$U_p(\beta,M,J)=\sum_{m=M}^{J}(m+1)^p e^{-\beta m^2} +\sum_{s=0}^{p}\binom ps I_s(J,\beta)$$
satisfies $T_p(\beta,M)\le U_p(\beta,M,J)$. Such a $J$ exists for every
$\beta>0$, $M\ge0$, and integer $p\ge0$.

derivations.claim: For $\alpha>0$ set $\mathcal R(\alpha)=\frac{QC_R}{\sqrt\pi\alpha}\sum_{m=M_R}^\infty(m+1)^3e^{-\alpha^2m^2}$ and $\mathcal K(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi QC_K}{V}\sum_{m=M_K}^\infty(m+1)^3e^{-m^2/(4\alpha^2)}$, where $M_R=\lfloor R\rfloor$ and $M_K=\lfloor K_c\rfloor$. These are exactly the two bounds in [F1], and they are finite by [F2].

If $0<\alpha_1<\alpha_2$, then for every $m\ge M_R\ge1$, $e^{-\alpha_2^2m^2}/\alpha_2<e^{-\alpha_1^2m^2}/\alpha_1$ because both positive factors strictly decrease. The positive convergent sum therefore gives $\mathcal R(\alpha_2)<\mathcal R(\alpha_1)$.

For every $m\ge M_K\ge1$, $e^{-m^2/(4\alpha_2^2)}>e^{-m^2/(4\alpha_1^2)}$, since $\alpha_2>\alpha_1$ makes the negative exponent less negative. Summing positive terms gives $\mathcal K(\alpha_2)>\mathcal K(\alpha_1)$. Hence a fixed-tolerance certificate must balance the real and reciprocal tails; the theorem does not infer an optimal parameter from FFT work or RMS data.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Use the periodic cardinal-assignment model of
[[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]], with integers $M_r\ge1$, order
$P\ge2$, grid size $N_g=\prod_rM_r$, a retained signed mode $k$ satisfying
$|k_r|<M_r/2$, and $D(k)\ne0$. Put $u_r=k_r/M_r$,
$a_k(t)=e^{-2\pi i k\cdot t}$, and
$$r_{k,n}=\prod_{r=1}^3 \frac{\overline{D_r(k_r+n_rM_r)}}{\overline{D_r(k_r)}},\qquad D_r(m)=e^{-\pi iPm/M_r}\operatorname{sinc}(\pi m/M_r)^P.$$
Then the single-particle assignment factor and the spread-grid coefficient obey
the absolutely convergent identities
$$b_k(t)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}r_{k,n}a_{k+n\odot M}(t),\qquad z_k=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}r_{k,n}\rho_{k+n\odot M},$$
where $(n\odot M)_r=n_rM_r$ and
$\rho_j=\sum_iq_i e^{-2\pi i j\cdot t_i}$. In particular
$$z_k-\rho_k=\sum_{n\ne0}r_{k,n}\rho_{k+n\odot M}.$$
The mesh coefficient also has the exact finite representation
$z_k=\sum_iq_i b_k(t_i)$, so no cell-volume or grid-size factor remains after
the displayed $\sqrt{N_g}$ conversion. The alias bound below uses only the Fourier series of
the compact spline; the lattice Poisson theorem is not applied to that spline.

For $u_r\ne0$ define
$$a_r(P,u_r)=\sum_{m\ne0}\left|\frac{u_r}{u_r+m}\right|^P, \qquad a_r(P,0)=0,\qquad A_k=\prod_{r=1}^3(1+a_r(P,u_r))-1.$$
Then $|b_k(t)-a_k(t)|\le A_k$, $|b_k(t)|\le1+A_k$, and
$|z_k-\rho_k|\le Q A_k$ for $Q=\sum_i|q_i|$. For $J\ge1$ and
$0<|u_r|<1/2$,
$$a_r(P,u_r)\le 2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\sum_{m=1}^\infty m^{-P},\qquad \sum_{|m|>J}\left|\frac{u_r}{u_r+m}\right|^P\le 2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\frac{\lfloor J\rfloor^{1-P}}{P-1}.$$
Thus every alias controller has a finite p-series remainder bound.
The periodic assignment also satisfies $\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t)=1$,
so the spread-grid zero mode is $\sum_{\ell}g_\ell=\sum_iq_i=0$ for neutral data.

Fix neutral point-source data $(A,V,\Lambda,\kappa_k,(x_i,q_i)_{i=1}^n)$ from
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]], an Ewald parameter
$\alpha>0$, integers $M_1,M_2,M_3\ge1$, an assignment order $P\ge2$, and write
$N_g=M_1M_2M_3$. Let $\mathcal G=\prod_{r=1}^3\{0,\ldots,M_r-1\}$ and take
$W_P$ from [[def-ewald-causal-cardinal-spline-window]]. Define the periodic
causal assignment weights, for $t\in[0,1)^3$ and $\ell\in\mathcal G$, by
$$w_\ell(t)=\prod_{r=1}^3\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z} W_P(M_rt_r-\ell_r-jM_r).$$
The sums are finite because $W_P$ is supported on $[0,P]$. They collect every
support index into its grid residue; if $P>M_r$, distinct support indices that
wrap to the same residue are added. The spread grid is
$$g_\ell=\sum_{i=1}^n q_iw_\ell(t_i),\qquad t_i=A^{-1}x_i\pmod{\mathbb Z^3}.$$

Use the negative-sign unitary tensor DFT convention
$$\widehat g_M(k)=N_g^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}g_\ell e^{-2\pi i\sum_{r=1}^3k_r\ell_r/M_r},$$
which is the product transform of
[[def-unitary-discrete-fourier-transform-on-z-mod-n]]. Signed frequency
representatives are chosen before evaluating windows. A retained set
$\mathcal K\subset\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$ is finite, symmetric under
$k\mapsto-k$, injective modulo $(M_1,M_2,M_3)$, and satisfies
$|k_r|<M_r/2$ for each coordinate. In particular, even-grid Nyquist modes are
not silently retained.

For $u\in\mathbb R$, put $\operatorname{sinc}(u)=\sin(u)/u$ when $u\ne0$ and
$\operatorname{sinc}(0)=1$. Define
$$D(k)=\prod_{r=1}^3e^{-\pi iPk_r/M_r} \operatorname{sinc}(\pi k_r/M_r)^P.$$
Only modes with $D(k)\ne0$ are admissible for division. A computed
implementation must first certify a strictly positive lower bound for
$|D(k)|$; otherwise it returns `denominator-inconclusive` without dividing.
For $k\in\mathcal K$, define
$$a_k(t)=e^{-2\pi i k\cdot t},\quad b_k(t)=\frac{\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t) e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}}{\overline{D(k)}},\quad \rho_k=\sum_iq_i a_k(t_i),\quad z_k=\frac{\sqrt{N_g}\,\widehat g_M(k)}{\overline{D(k)}}.$$
The denominator is the complex conjugate of the printed window multiplier; this
sign is part of the definition. Set
$$c_k=\frac{4\pi}{V|\kappa_k|^2} e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}.$$
The exact retained reciprocal energy is
$$E_{\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|\rho_k|^2,$$
and the mesh reciprocal energy is
$$E_M=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|z_k|^2.$$

Let $\mathfrak d_k(t)$ be the declared physical mesh derivative: it is
$\nabla_xb_k(t)=A^{-T}\nabla_tb_k(t)$ wherever the classical derivative
exists. A grid knot is a point with $M_rt_r\in\mathbb Z$ for some coordinate
$r$. At a $P=2$ knot, take the one-sided vector limits from all adjacent open
mesh boxes. Define $\mathfrak d_k(t)$ to be any selected one-sided limit or the
arithmetic average of all those limits. This is a procedure value and does not
assert that the classical derivative exists there. The
energy-gradient mesh force is
$$F_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\overline{z_k}\mathfrak d_k(t_i)\right).$$
Define the diagonal mesh-self correction and corrected reciprocal energy by
$$C_M=\frac12\sum_iq_i^2\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k (|b_k(t_i)|^2-1),\qquad E_M^{\mathrm{corr}}=E_M-C_M.$$
Whether the declared force is the derivative of this corrected energy, and the
error bound it satisfies, are proved separately.

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite source data on the cell $A\mathbb Z^3$
from [[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Fix $\alpha>0$,
integers $M_r\ge1$, an order $P\ge2$, and a finite symmetric set
$\mathcal K\subset\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$ whose signed representatives are
injective modulo $(M_1,M_2,M_3)$ and satisfy $|k_r|<M_r/2$. Require $D(k)\ne0$
for every $k\in\mathcal K$, and let $c_k=4\pi e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}/(V|\kappa_k|^2)$ be the positive Ewald coefficient. Use the assignment factors $a_k,b_k,\rho_k,z_k$ of [[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]], and put $Q=\sum_j|q_j|$.

For a query point $x$ write $t=A^{-1}x$ modulo $\mathbb Z^3$ and define the retained exact and mesh reciprocal potentials by
$$U_{\mathcal K}(x)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\rho_k\overline{a_k(t)}),\qquad U_{M,\mathcal K}(x)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(z_k\overline{b_k(t)}).$$
Define $E_{\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|\rho_k|^2$ and $E_{M,\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|z_k|^2$. For each mode let $A_k$ be the source-alias controller in [[lem-ewald-pme-spline-alias-and-dft-normalization]], and let $B_k$ be the derivative-alias controller in [[lem-ewald-pme-derivative-window-alias-bound]].

Let a complex-vector derivative/gather value $d_k(t)$ satisfy $\|d_k(t)-\mathfrak d_k(t)\|_2\le H_k$ for a stated $H_k\ge0$, where $\mathfrak d_k$ is the declared derivative branch of [[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]] and $\nabla_x=A^{-T}\nabla_t$. The uncorrected mesh and exact reciprocal forces are
$$F^d_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{z_k}d_k(t_i)),\qquad F_{\mathcal K,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\rho_k}\nabla_xa_k(t_i)).$$
Then for every query point $x$,
$$|U_{M,\mathcal K}(x)-U_{\mathcal K}(x)|\le Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k),\qquad |E_{M,\mathcal K}-E_{\mathcal K}|\le\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k),$$
and for every particle $i$,
$$\|F^d_{M,i}-F_{\mathcal K,i}\|_2\le |q_i|Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\bigl[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k+(1+A_k)H_k\bigr].$$

For the declared energy-gradient gather $d_k=\mathfrak d_k$ (so $H_k=0$), the mesh force is $-\nabla_{x_i}E_{M,\mathcal K}$ wherever the classical derivative exists. This holds everywhere for $P\ge3$ and off the assignment knots for $P=2$; at a $P=2$ knot the selected one-sided derivative or its average is a procedure value, with the same bound but without a differentiability claim.

The optional diagonal self correction is
$$C_M=\frac12\sum_iq_i^2\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k(|b_k(t_i)|^2-1),\qquad E^{\rm corr}_{M,\mathcal K}=E_{M,\mathcal K}-C_M.$$
For its finite cyclic implementation, set $h_k=c_k/|D(k)|^2$ on $\mathcal K$,
$$\gamma_d=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}h_ke^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_rd_r/M_r},\qquad S_i=\sum_{\ell,m\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t_i)w_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}.$$
Then $\gamma$ is real and even, $S_i=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|b_k(t_i)|^2$, and, on every differentiable branch (or as the same declared one-sided branch at a $P=2$ knot),
$$\nabla_{x_i}(S_i/2)=\sum_{\ell,m\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t_i)\nabla_xw_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}.$$
Consequently this local cyclic-kernel expression computes $C_M$ and its derivative exactly in real arithmetic.
The finite tensor-transform gathers also have the exact real-arithmetic forms
$$U_{M,\mathcal K}(x)=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t_x)u_\ell,\qquad u_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\frac{c_kz_k}{D(k)}e^{2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r},$$
$$F_{M,i}=-q_i\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}\lambda_\ell\nabla_xw_\ell(t_i),\qquad \lambda_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\frac{c_k\overline{z_k}}{\overline{D(k)}}e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}.$$
These identities hold with the declared derivative branch, including the selected one-sided $P=2$ knot value.
It satisfies
$$|E^{\rm corr}_{M,\mathcal K}-E_{\mathcal K}|\le\frac{Q^2-\sum_iq_i^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k).$$
In the energy-gradient branch its exactly differentiated force is
$$F^{\rm corr}_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\overline{z_k-q_ib_k(t_i)}\,\mathfrak d_k(t_i)\bigr),$$
and
$$\|F^{\rm corr}_{M,i}-F_{\mathcal K,i}\|_2\le |q_i|(Q-|q_i|)\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\bigl[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k\bigr].$$
The corrected force is the negative classical energy gradient in the same differentiable cases; at a $P=2$ knot it is only the declared branch value. No pointwise error estimate here replaces an RMS estimate, and no claim is made that a different spectral differentiation rule is the gradient of the mesh energy.

abla_xb_k(t_i))$. Summing over $k\in\mathcal K$ and negating yields exactly the stated energy-gradient force. [F1, F2, algebra]
