Assume Countable Choice. Inputs are a full-rank real cell matrix $A$, a finite
neutral configuration of pairwise-distinct torus positions $x_i$ and real
charges $q_i$, an Ewald parameter $\alpha>0$, cutoffs $R,K_c\ge1$, integers
$M_r\ge1$, an order $P\ge2$, a mesh-self-correction flag, an optional off-source
query point $x$, requested nonnegative tolerances for each requested output,
and integer controller indices $J_R\ge\lfloor R\rfloor$,
$J_K\ge\lfloor K_c\rfloor$, and $J_A\ge1$. The inputs must satisfy
$2\alpha^2J_R(J_R+1)\ge3$ and
$(2\alpha^2)^{-1}J_K(J_K+1)\ge3$ for the shell controllers. The arithmetic
interface is one fixed instance of
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]],
with representable set $\mathbb F$ and certified outward enclosures for every
finite arithmetic node, elementary-function evaluation, transform phase, and
final arithmetic radius. There is an optional positive integer enclosure-work
cap $B_{\mathrm{encl}}$, defaulting to $1$ when omitted. Each non-transform
validation, enclosure, or comparison request executes its supplied certificate
lookup/evaluation program for at most $B_{\mathrm{encl}}$ program
instructions, including control-flow steps. Its numerical primitives are exact
rational arithmetic/comparisons, fixed-format rounded operations, and reads of
finite supplied certificate data. Elementary functions
and refinement loops are implemented through these counted instructions, not
as uncapped oracle calls. On exhaustion, unavailable data, a nonfinite bound,
an uncertified required divisor or an unresolved comparison, return
`arithmetic-inconclusive`, except where an explicit cutoff, transform, or
window-denominator branch below names its more specific status. Do not retry
with larger budgets inside a run. A larger cap may be supplied for another
run; no accepted enclosure loses its required soundness. Supplied finite
certificate data and the cap are part of the arithmetic interface, so this
rule does not impose a precision or accuracy restriction on successful outputs. Every particle and optional query point also has a
certified representative interval in $[0,1)^3$ after reduction modulo the
cell. Transform calls use common controls: an exact rational phase tolerance
$\tau$ with $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer exponent limits $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$,
integer precision $p_0\ge2$, finite integer cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, integer
elementary-series cap $J_{\mathrm{phase}}\ge1$, and integer radix-two depth
$d_{\max}\ge0$ required by
[[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]]. Every vector passed to a
transform has real and imaginary coordinates in $\mathbb F$, and the outward
enclosures include phase and arithmetic errors from the entire transform call.
If $\sum_iq_i\ne0$ is certified, return `nonneutral`. Otherwise check
neutrality, distinctness, full rank, valid scalar/integer controls, and the
required input enclosures using the bounded interface above. A certified
violation of these input conditions returns `invalid-input`; unavailable or
unresolved evidence returns `arithmetic-inconclusive`. If a query point is
certified to be a source image, return `collision` for that potential query;
if its off-source status is unresolved, return `arithmetic-inconclusive`.
A controller inequality that is certified false is `invalid-input`; an
unresolved one is `arithmetic-inconclusive`.

1. Compute a certified outward upper bound $B_K$ for $\|A^T\|_2K_c/(2\pi)$ and set $N_K=\lceil B_K\rceil$. Enumerate every integer triple in the finite box $[-N_K,N_K]^3$. For each nonzero $k$, compute a certified interval $[d_k^-,d_k^+]$ for $|2\pi A^{-T}k|$ and an interval $[K_c^-,K_c^+]$ for $K_c$. Include $k$ in $\mathcal B_{K_c}$ if $d_k^+\le K_c^-$, exclude it if $d_k^->K_c^+$, and return `cutoff-inconclusive` if neither comparison is certified. Retain from $\mathcal B_{K_c}$ exactly the signed modes satisfying $|k_r|<M_r/2$ for every coordinate and store them in $\mathcal K$. This set is finite, symmetric and injective modulo the mesh. Every other mode in $\mathcal B_{K_c}$ is kept in the finite omitted-mode ledger $\mathcal M_{K_c}=\mathcal B_{K_c}\setminus\mathcal K$; it is never assigned zero error.

2. Initialize the full grid $g$ to zero. Use each particle's supplied certified representative interval $t_i\in[0,1)^3$. For each coordinate $r$, enclose $a=M_rt_{i,r}$ by $[a^-,a^+]$; if $a^+-a^->1$, return `arithmetic-inconclusive`. Enumerate every integer $L_r$ from $\lceil a^- -P\rceil$ through $\lfloor a^+\rfloor$. This finite list contains every translate with $0\le a-L_r\le P$ and has at most $P+2$ entries. For every triple $(L_1,L_2,L_3)$, evaluate $q_i\prod_rW_P(M_rt_{i,r}-L_r)$, reduce $L_r$ modulo $M_r$ to the grid residue $\ell_r$, add the term to $g_\ell$, and store the particle's finite support tuples for later gathers. This Cartesian list computes the periodic assignment exactly because each integer $L_r$ is uniquely $\ell_r+jM_r$. Accumulate all terms that wrap to the same residue; when $P>M_r$, do not drop duplicate contributions. The support is the causal predecessor support of the window, not an unspecified symmetric nearest-node rule.

3. For each coordinate fiber, call [[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]] with the supplied common transform controls on its representable center vector. If an input cannot be represented, a call returns any `inconclusive` or `range-failure` status, or a normalization scale fails, return `transform-inconclusive` and retain that substatus. Apply the negative-sign unitary tensor DFT
$$\widehat g_M(k)=N_g^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}g_\ell e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r},\qquad N_g=M_1M_2M_3,$$
by dividing each returned unnormalised coordinate transform by $\sqrt{M_r}$, with outward enclosures for every scale operation. The required mathematical output convention is the unitary transform. The correctness-and-cost supplier proves the formal exact-constant transform identity; it is not used as a floating-point error bound.

4. For each retained $k$, form the window multiplier
$$D(k)=\prod_{r=1}^3e^{-\pi iPk_r/M_r}\operatorname{sinc}(\pi k_r/M_r)^P$$
and obtain an outward lower bound for $|D(k)|$. If any lower bound is nonpositive, return `denominator-inconclusive` without division. Otherwise set
$$z_k=\frac{\sqrt{N_g}\,\widehat g_M(k)}{\overline{D(k)}},\qquad c_k=\frac{4\pi e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}}{V|\kappa_k|^2}.$$
Use the conjugated denominator forced by the negative-sign DFT and the causal window. The signed mode representative is used in every window factor; residues are used only as storage indices.

5. For every tensor-transform call in this step, use [[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]] with the same model and controls as in Step 3, divide each coordinate output by $\sqrt{M_r}$, and propagate a failed or unrepresentable subcall or failed normalization as `transform-inconclusive`. Form mode arrays on the full mesh-frequency grid, placing retained signed modes in their unique residues and setting all other entries to zero. Set $v^U_k=c_kz_k/D(k)$ on $\mathcal K$. Apply the per-coordinate unitary normalization to the negative-sign tensor DFT of $\overline{v^U}$, conjugate the output, and multiply by $\sqrt{N_g}$; the inverse-transform target array is $u_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}v^U_ke^{2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}$. If a query point was supplied, use its supplied representative $t_x$ and the finite-support routine of Step 2 to compute the off-source mesh potential $\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t_x)u_\ell$. For forces set $v^F_k=c_k\overline{z_k}/\overline{D(k)}$ on $\mathcal K$, zero elsewhere, and apply the same per-coordinate normalization to its negative-sign tensor DFT, then multiply by $\sqrt{N_g}$ to form $\lambda_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}v^F_ke^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}$. Evaluate $\nabla_xw_\ell$ by differentiating the finite support products on the selected mesh box and applying $A^{-T}$; aggregate all tuple derivative contributions by residue, retaining duplicate wraps. Then $F_{M,i}=-q_i\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}\lambda_\ell\nabla_xw_\ell(t_i)$, gathering only the at most $(P+2)^3$ candidate support contributions per particle. For $P=2$ at a knot, use the one-sided derivative from the adjacent box immediately to the right in each knot coordinate (box index $\lfloor M_rt_r\rfloor$ modulo $M_r$), consistently for the full derivative vector and both correction factors. Determine this right-hand mesh-box index by the bounded certificate interface, allowing a supplied exact knot equality; if its floor/branch cannot be certified, return `arithmetic-inconclusive`. This is the selected branch from the assignment definition and is not asserted to be a classical gradient. Computed enclosures retain outward bounds on residual imaginary parts. The mesh energy is $E_{M,\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|z_k|^2$.

   If mesh-self correction is enabled, place $h_k=c_k/|D(k)|^2$ on retained residues and zero elsewhere. Apply the same normalized negative-sign tensor DFT to $h$ and multiply by $\sqrt{N_g}$ to form the cyclic kernel $\gamma_d=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}h_ke^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_rd_r/M_r}$. For each particle evaluate $S_i=\sum_{\ell,m}w_\ell(t_i)w_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}$ over all support-residue pairs, retaining duplicate-wrap contributions, and set $C_M=\frac12\sum_iq_i^2(S_i-\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k)$. Replace the mesh energy by $E_{M,\mathcal K}-C_M$. Replace the uncorrected force by $F_{M,i}+q_i^2\sum_{\ell,m}w_\ell(t_i)\nabla_xw_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}$, using the same selected derivative branch. The equality of this finite cyclic-kernel computation with the correction and its branch derivative is proved in [[thm-ewald-pme-reciprocal-energy-force-error-bound]]. Outward enclosures include the kernel transform, local products, derivative-window factors, and subtraction.

6. For each query/particle pair and particle pair, use certified representatives $t_a,t_b\in[0,1)^3$. If $|A(t_a-t_b+\ell)|\le R$, then $|\ell|\le\|A^{-1}\|_2R+\sqrt3$. Compute an outward upper bound $B_R$ for the right-hand side, set $N_R=\lceil B_R\rceil$, and for each required query or particle pair enumerate every integer index in $[-N_R,N_R]^3$. For each candidate compute an outward interval $[r^-,r^+]$ for its image distance and an interval $[R^-,R^+]$ for $R$; include the image if $r^+\le R^-$, exclude it if $r^->R^+$, and return `cutoff-inconclusive` otherwise. Use these finite lists to compute the real potential when requested, real energy, and real force, excluding exactly the own zero-image term $(j,\ell)=(i,0)$ from energy and force before any singular kernel division. For every other retained image certify a positive lower distance bound before dividing; otherwise return `arithmetic-inconclusive`. Keep the force convention as the finite sum of differentiated retained pair kernels; do not differentiate the hard-cutoff membership indicator. Add the ordinary Ewald energy constant $-\alpha\sum_iq_i^2/\sqrt\pi$ to the total energy. The point-source potential is only returned off all source images.

7. Compute $M_R=\lfloor R\rfloor$ and $M_K=\lfloor K_c\rfloor$; if either floor is not determined by its certified enclosure, return `cutoff-inconclusive`. Construct finite $U_3$ real and reciprocal shell controllers with the supplied $J_R,J_K$. For each retained mode, compute outward bounds for $A_k$ and $B_k$ by summing the source/derivative alias terms through $|n_r|\le J_A$ and adding the supplier's finite p-series remainders; for $P=2$, use its finite derivative-window controller. Use $H_k=0$ for the declared analytic-window gather in both force branches; place all finite arithmetic errors in the supplied radii $\varepsilon_{F,i}$. Include every omitted mode in $\mathcal M_{K_c}$ and the mesh-self correction if enabled. Add the actual outward arithmetic radii for all spread, transform, solve, gather, summation, and correction nodes. The outward enclosures for finite controllers themselves use the bounded enclosure interface above; its name does not authorize an unbounded oracle or refinement search. If a required arithmetic radius or controller enclosure is unavailable, return `arithmetic-inconclusive`. Otherwise retain the computed intervals and total error radii for the final output. Use the same bounded interface for tolerance comparisons: return `certified` when every requested radius is certified to meet its tolerance, `certified-over-tolerance` when at least one is certified to exceed it, and `arithmetic-inconclusive` if neither decision is certified. The total-certificate theorem proves the error bounds and formal operation-count properties for this evaluation; operation counts do not certify accuracy.

Input an exact rational $q$, an exact rational target $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer dyadic exponent limits $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$, an initial precision $p_0\ge2$, a finite precision cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, and a finite elementary-series cap $J\ge1$. The target value is $w=e^{\pi iq}=\cos(\pi q)+i\sin(\pi q)$ by [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], for the canonical Fourier $\pi$ identified with the interval evaluator's constant by [[thm-na-interval-pi-matches-canonical-fourier-pi]]. For each precision $p=p_0,p_0+1,\ldots,p_{\max}$, and $t\in\{1/5,1/239\}$, form the exact rational interval $I_J(t)=[A_J(t)-R_J(t),A_J(t)+R_J(t)]$, where
$$A_J(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{J}\frac{(-1)^jt^{2j+1}}{2j+1},\qquad R_J(t)=\frac{|t|^{2J+3}}{(2J+3)(1-t^2)}.$$
The Machin identity gives the interval $P=16I_J(1/5)-4I_J(1/239)$ containing $\pi$. Form the exact rational interval $qP$ by taking the minimum and maximum of its two endpoint products, then round its endpoints down and up to obtain a dyadic input interval $\Theta$ in format $(p,e_{\min},e_{\max})$. If this conversion overflows, treat that precision as a non-finite evaluation. Otherwise build two finite real expression DAGs with input interval $\Theta$ and requested outputs $\cos(\Theta)$ and $\sin(\Theta)$, and call [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] using the same dyadic format and truncation index $J$; its fixed finite-cell rules govern range reduction. If either result is non-finite, continue at the next precision unless the precision cap is reached, in which case return `inconclusive` with the supplier status. If the results are finite intervals $C=[c_-,c_+]$ and $S=[s_-,s_+]$, set $\widehat w=c_-+is_-$ and compute an upward-rounded dyadic $\epsilon\ge(c_+-c_-)+(s_+-s_-)$. If $\epsilon\le\tau$, return `certified(\widehat w,\epsilon)`; otherwise continue or return `inconclusive` at the cap. A non-finite endpoint or overflow returns its explicit failure status. The routine makes no finite-error claim on a failure branch.

Input: a finite, well-formed, typed expression DAG with one or more designated
output nodes; finite real interval or complex rectangle assignments for its
input nodes; exact dyadic constants or constants supplied with certified
enclosing intervals/rectangles; a finite dyadic format $(p,e_{\min},e_{\max})$
with $p\ge2$ and $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$; and an integer truncation index
$N\ge1$. Input interval endpoints and supplied constant enclosures use this
format. All constants, including every Machin enclosure of $\pi$, use the
same fixed $N$ and format throughout a call. Real nodes support input and
constant nodes and the operations $+,-,\times,\div,\sqrt{\phantom{x}},
\exp,\ln,\arctan,\sin,\cos,\tan$. Complex nodes support input and constant
nodes and $+,-,\times,\div,\exp,\operatorname{Log}$. Each operation has
homogeneous real or complex inputs of its stated type; no implicit conversion
between real and complex nodes is performed. Unsupported node types, arities,
or type combinations return `inconclusive` with the offending node.

Output: a finite interval/rectangle enclosure for every designated output
node, or one of `empty`, `entire`, `domain-error`, `split-domain`, `overflow`,
or `inconclusive` with the node and unresolved domain piece. If any supplied
input is `empty`, return `empty`. No value from a system `libm` routine is
treated as a certified endpoint. Each DAG node is evaluated once; shared nodes
reuse their interval/rectangle enclosure and do not preserve correlations
between distinct paths.

1. Check that node identifiers are unique, all references resolve, every
designated output is a node, and the supported node types and arities above
hold. Use each supplied input enclosure as its node value. For an exact real
dyadic constant $c$, use $[\operatorname{rd}(c),\operatorname{ru}(c)]$ in the
selected format. For an exact complex dyadic constant, do this to each
coordinate. A finite subnormal endpoint remains a valid endpoint; if a
coordinate conversion overflows, return `overflow` with that constant node.
Use a supplied certified constant enclosure as given. Construct a topological
order by repeatedly removing a node whose
predecessors have already been removed, breaking ties by lexicographically
smallest node identifier. If no such node exists before all nodes are ordered,
return `inconclusive` with a node in the cycle. Evaluate nodes in this order
and store each finite enclosure for its successors. Arithmetic nodes use
[[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]]; if an operation returns
a non-finite status, propagate it immediately with its node and unresolved
piece. For $\sqrt{X}$ require $X\subseteq[0,\infty)$ and for $\ln X$ require
$X\subseteq(0,\infty)$; otherwise return `domain-error` rather than silently
discarding points.

2. For a real exponential node, set $s=\max(0,e_{\max}+2)$ using the format
in [[def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding]]. Since
$N_{\max}<2^{e_{\max}+1}$, exact comparison gives $N_{\max}/2^s<1/2$. For
its input interval $X$, form the exact dyadic interval $U=2^{-s}X$
without storage rounding. Evaluate the degree-$N$ exponential polynomial and
add the symmetric tail from
[[lem-range-reduced-exp-log-and-arctan-series-enclosures]], using
$\max_{u\in U}|u|<1/2$, by exact rational interval arithmetic. Round only
the resulting interval endpoints outward, then square that interval $s$ times. If its lower
endpoint is not positive or an endpoint overflows, return `inconclusive` or
`overflow` with the node and input interval.

For a real logarithm node, first require $X\subseteq(0,\infty)$. List all
integers $j$ for which $X_j=X\cap[2^j,2^{j+1}]$ is nonempty; exact endpoint
comparisons find this finite list because $X$ has positive finite endpoints.
On each piece form $Y=2^{-j}X_j\subseteq[1,2]$ and $V=(Y-1)/(Y+1)$
by exact rational endpoint formulas without storage rounding, so
$V\subseteq[0,1/3]$. Evaluate the logarithm polynomial and its tail
determined by $\max|V|$ by exact rational interval arithmetic, round the
result outward, and form $j\ln2+\ln Y$ by outward arithmetic. Compute the fixed enclosure for
$\ln2$ once by the same series and tail at $y=2$, hence $v=1/3$, and reuse it
in every bin. If any piece cannot be evaluated finitely, propagate its status
and that piece. Otherwise take the interval hull of all piece enclosures as
the node enclosure.

3. Partition a real arctangent input at the fixed breakpoints
$-3,-1,-1/2,1/2,1,3$ into nonempty closed pieces, allowing shared endpoints.
On pieces in $[-1/2,1/2]$, evaluate its alternating power series. For positive
pieces in $[1/2,1]$, use
$\arctan t=\pi/4-\arctan((1-t)/(1+t))$; in $[1,3]$, use
$\arctan t=\pi/4+\arctan((t-1)/(t+1))$; for $t\ge3$, use
$\arctan t=\pi/2-\arctan(1/t)$. Evaluate negative pieces by odd symmetry. Form each reduced interval by
exact rational endpoint formulas and evaluate its polynomial and symmetric
tail by exact rational interval arithmetic before outward conversion; every
reduced argument lies in $[-1/2,1/2]$. Combine the converted enclosure with
the fixed $\pi$ enclosure by outward arithmetic. Enclose $\pi$ using Machin's identity and the alternating series at $1/5$ and
$1/239$, forming rational partial sums and tail endpoints exactly before
final outward conversion. If every piece is finite, take the interval hull of
all piece enclosures. If any branch test or piece is unresolved, return its
non-finite status with that piece and do not use a partial hull.

4. For each sine or cosine node, first compute one outward Machin interval
$P_N$ for $\pi$ using the same $N$ and format, combining the rational series
endpoints exactly before final outward conversion. If $P_N$ is non-finite or
its lower endpoint is not positive, return `inconclusive`. For finite input
$X=[a,b]$, put $M_X=\max(|a|,|b|)$, $p_-:=\inf(P_N)>0$, and
$K=\lceil2M_X/p_-\rceil+1$, with the ceiling computed by exact rational
comparisons. If the width of $X$ is at least $2\sup(P_N)$, outward-round the
exact endpoints $-1$ and $1$; if either conversion overflows, return
`overflow` with the node and input interval, and otherwise return the resulting
interval. Otherwise examine the finite candidate list $k=-K,\ldots,K$ for
the canonical cells $[k\pi/2-\pi/4,k\pi/2+\pi/4]$. For each candidate form
the exact rational interval enclosure
$C_k=kP_N/2+[-1/4,1/4]P_N$ of its canonical cell. For $k>K$, the exact
left endpoint $(2k-1)\pi/4$ of cell $k$ is at least
$(2k-1)p_-/4>M_X$; for $k<-K$, its exact right endpoint
$-(2|k|-1)\pi/4$ is at most $-(2|k|-1)p_-/4<-M_X$. Thus no omitted exact
cell can intersect $X$. Include each candidate whose $C_k$ intersects $X$;
exclude only candidates whose intersection is empty by exact comparison. Let
$X_k$ be the exact interval hull of $X\cap C_k$, without rounding these
endpoints, and form the residual enclosure $R_k=X_k-kP_N/2$. Certify
$R_k\subseteq[-1,1]$, evaluate the sine polynomial through degree $2N+1$ or
the cosine polynomial through degree $2N$, and add the corresponding explicit
geometric tail from [[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]]
by exact rational interval arithmetic. For $j\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ the
quarter-period map for a sine node is respectively
$\sin r,\cos r,-\sin r,-\cos r$, and for a cosine node it is respectively
$\cos r,-\sin r,-\cos r,\sin r$, where $j$ is the least nonnegative residue
of $k$ modulo $4$. For a negative sign, negate the interval and reverse its
endpoints. Intersect each mapped enclosure with $[-1,1]$. Round the final
endpoints outward and take the hull over every included cell.
If no candidate is included, a cell cannot be certified in the reduced
interval, or any candidate endpoint overflows, return `inconclusive` or
`overflow` with the cell; never omit that piece from a finite hull.

For tangent, form the same finite canonical-cell list even when the input width
meets the wide-input shortcut; do not use that shortcut. For each included cell
$k$, form its reduced input interval $R_k$ as above and evaluate sine and
cosine on that cell. Divide their enclosures only when the cosine enclosure
excludes zero. Otherwise, for odd $k$, form the exact dyadic pole enclosure
$K_k=kP_N/2$. If $K_k$ is contained in the cell's input intersection, then
$k\pi/2$ lies in that cell and is a cosine zero, so return `split-domain` with
the cell. If the cosine enclosure contains zero but this pole test does not
certify a zero, return `inconclusive` with the cell. Take the interval hull of
tangent enclosures only when every piece is finite.

5. For complex exponential on $X+iY$, evaluate real $\exp(X)$, $\cos(Y)$,
and $\sin(Y)$ and combine their enclosures by rectangle operations. For
principal $\operatorname{Log}$, first require a rectangle excluding zero and
every point of the negative real branch cut; otherwise return `domain-error`.
Compute an outward Machin interval $P_N$ for $\pi$ using this call's $N$ and
format; if it is non-finite or its lower endpoint is not positive, return
`inconclusive`.
Split each coordinate interval into its nonempty strictly negative and
strictly positive portions, plus the singleton $\{0\}$ when it contains zero.
Use the closures of the strictly signed portions as interval enclosures; form
their Cartesian products for the quadrant pieces, and handle products with an
axis singleton separately. Omit empty pieces. These finitely many pieces
cover the rectangle, with quadrant closures allowed to overlap their axis
pieces. On a quadrant where the denominator interval excludes zero, use
$$\operatorname{Arg}(x+iy)= \begin{cases} \arctan(y/x),&x>0,\ y>0,\\ -\arctan((-y)/x),&x>0,\ y<0,\\ \pi-\arctan(y/(-x)),&x<0,\ y>0,\\ -\pi+\arctan((-y)/(-x)),&x<0,\ y<0. \end{cases}$$
Write this call's fixed interval as $P_N=[p_-,p_+]$ and form the exact
dyadic sector intervals
$$S_{\rm I}=[0,p_+/2],\qquad S_{\rm II}=[p_-/2,p_+],\qquad S_{\rm III}=[-p_+,-p_-/2],\qquad S_{\rm IV}=[-p_+/2,0].$$
For every ratio-based quadrant piece, obtain its finite real arctangent
enclosure by the real rules above; propagate any non-finite result. Form the
full argument interval $A$ in the displayed quadrant formula by exact
rational endpoint arithmetic, using this same $P_N$ for each occurrence of
$\pi$. Before final outward conversion or hull formation, replace $A$ by
$J=A\cap S_q$, where $q$ is that piece's quadrant. Compute the intersection
by exact endpoint maxima and minima. If it is empty, return `inconclusive`
with the piece and status `empty-argument-intersection`; do not omit the
piece. If the denominator interval has a zero endpoint, use $J=S_q$
instead of a ratio formula.

For an interval $J=[a,b]$ produced by either branch, apply the same final
conversion $H(J)=[\operatorname{rd}(a),\operatorname{ru}(b)]$ in the selected
format. Perform this conversion after intersection for a ratio branch and
after selecting $S_q$ for a coarse branch. Finite subnormal endpoints are
accepted; an overflow returns `overflow` with the piece. On the positive
imaginary axis use $H(P_N/2)$, on the negative imaginary axis use
$H(-P_N/2)$, and on the positive real axis use $H([0,0])$. The initial domain
check excludes the origin and negative real axis, so these are all remaining
axis cases.

On each piece enclose $\ln\sqrt{X^2+Y^2}$ using the real operations and
evaluator, and combine it with the converted argument interval into a
rectangle. If every piece is finite, take the coordinatewise hull of all
piece rectangles. If any piece, conversion or branch is unresolved, return
its status and piece without forming a partial hull.

Input: a nonnegative exact dyadic rational $x$ and integer request $n\ge1$.
Output: an exact dyadic lower and upper bound for $\sqrt{x}$; no finite
storage format is needed by this procedure.

1. If $x=0$, return $[0,0]$.
2. Otherwise determine the unique integer $j$ with $2^j\le x<2^{j+1}$ from the
   exact dyadic representation, put $m=\lfloor j/2\rfloor$ and
   $\delta=2^{m-n}$.
3. Set integer indices $L=0$ and $U=2^{n+1}$. While $U-L>1$, put
   $Q=\lfloor(L+U)/2\rfloor$. If $(Q\delta)^2\le x$, replace $L$ by $Q$;
   otherwise replace $U$ by $Q$.
4. Return the exact dyadic pair $[L\delta,U\delta]$. A caller that stores
   these endpoints in a selected finite format must separately round the
   lower endpoint down and the upper endpoint up, propagating the resulting
   `subnormal` or `overflow` status.

All comparisons and multiplications in the loop are exact integer/dyadic
operations.

For real intervals $X=[a,b]$ and $Y=[c,d]$, compute the displayed exact
endpoint formulas and round the lower endpoint down and the upper endpoint up
in the format of
[[def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding]]. If either exact
endpoint overflows, return `overflow` with the outward extended endpoints;
never substitute a finite endpoint for an overflow sentinel. Addition is
$[a+c,b+d]$, subtraction is $[a-d,b-c]$, and multiplication is
$[\min(ac,ad,bc,bd),\max(ac,ad,bc,bd)]$. Division is defined only when
$0\notin Y$ and is $X[1/d,1/c]$, with reciprocal endpoints computed as exact
rationals before outward rounding. Squaring is
$[0,\max(a^2,b^2)]$ when $0\in X$ and
$[\min(a^2,b^2),\max(a^2,b^2)]$ otherwise. Square root is defined only for
$X\subseteq[0,\infty)$ and is enclosed by applying
[[alg-dyadic-square-root-bisection]] to the exact dyadic endpoints with
request $n=p$, where $p$ is the selected format precision, and rounding
outward for storage.

If $0\in Y$ for division, return `split-domain` with the two subdomains
$Y\cap(-\infty,0)$ and $Y\cap(0,\infty)$, or `entire` when the caller does not
request subdivision. No finite quotient interval is returned in this case.
An invalid square-root domain returns `domain-error` or an explicitly
restricted nonnegative subdomain.

Complex-rectangle addition, subtraction and multiplication use
$(x+iy)(u+iv)=(xu-yv)+i(xv+yu)$, applying the real interval operations to
each component. For a rectangle $X+iY$ excluding $0$, define its reciprocal by
$(X-iY)/(X^2+Y^2)$, computing the square hulls, their sum, and the
component quotient endpoint formulas as exact rationals before rounding the
final reciprocal components outward. The exact denominator interval is
strictly positive because at least one coordinate interval excludes zero;
do not round it before division, since underflow could introduce zero.
Propagate any final endpoint overflow. Division multiplies by this reciprocal.

For a ball $B(c,r)$, let $X_B=[\Re c-r,\Re c+r]$ and
$Y_B=[\Im c-r,\Im c+r]$ be its coordinate projection intervals. For a real
interval $J$, let $M(J)=\max(|\inf J|,|\sup J|)$ and let $d(J)=0$ if
$0\in J$, otherwise $d(J)=\min(|\inf J|,|\sup J|)$. Put
$M_B=M(X_B)+M(Y_B)$ and $m_B=\max(d(X_B),d(Y_B))$. Then
$|z|\le M_B$ for every $z\in B(c,r)$ and $|z|\ge m_B$ for every such $z$.
Define ball addition and subtraction as
$B(0,\operatorname{ru}(M_{B_1}+M_{B_2}))$, multiplication as
$B(0,\operatorname{ru}(M_{B_1}M_{B_2}))$, and division as
$B(0,\operatorname{ru}(M_{B_1}/m_{B_2}))$ only when $m_{B_2}>0$. These
origin-centered output balls are conservative but inclusion-isotone. If
$m_{B_2}=0$, return `split-domain`, `entire`, or `inconclusive`; if a radius
overlows, return `overflow`.

An exact dyadic rational is a number $m2^q$ with integers $m,q$.
Fix integers $p\ge2$ and $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$. Put
$\eta=2^{e_{\min}-p+1}$ and
$N_{\max}=(2^p-1)2^{e_{\max}-p+1}$. The finite representable set $\mathbb F$
consists of zero, both signs of every normal number $k2^{e-p+1}$ with integers $e,k$ satisfying
$e_{\min}\le e\le e_{\max}$ and $2^{p-1}\le k<2^p$, and both signs of every
subnormal number $k\eta$ with integer $k$ satisfying $1\le k<2^{p-1}$. The smallest positive
subnormal is $\eta$, the smallest positive normal is $2^{e_{\min}}$, and the
largest finite magnitude is $N_{\max}$. The extended endpoint set also contains
$-\infty$ and $+\infty$ as enclosure sentinels; they are not finite machine
numbers.

For a real $x$ with $|x|\le N_{\max}$, define $\operatorname{rd}(x)$ as the
greatest member of $\mathbb F$ not exceeding $x$, and $\operatorname{ru}(x)$ as
the least member of $\mathbb F$ not less than $x$. Define
$\rho(x)=\operatorname{ru}(x)-\operatorname{rd}(x)$. Set $\epsilon_{\rm abs}(0)=0$.
For nonzero $x$ in the
subnormal range, define the absolute-error bound $\epsilon_{\rm abs}(x)=\eta$;
for $2^e\le |x|<2^{e+1}$ in the normal range, define
$\epsilon_{\rm abs}(x)=2^{e-p+2}$. For $x>N_{\max}$, set
$(\operatorname{rd}(x),\operatorname{ru}(x))=(N_{\max},+\infty)$; for
$x<-N_{\max}$, set
$(\operatorname{rd}(x),\operatorname{ru}(x))=(-\infty,-N_{\max})$.
In either overflow case set $\epsilon_{\rm abs}(x)=+\infty$ and report
`overflow`, even when the selected directed endpoint is finite.
The rounding procedure reports `finite`, `subnormal`, or
`overflow`, so no relative-error assumption is implicit.

An exact rational intermediate may be converted by comparing integer
numerators and denominators after clearing powers of two. A directed interval
endpoint is the resulting greatest lower or least upper member of the
extended endpoint set $\mathbb F\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$.

Fix an instance of the operationwise floating-point model in [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], with representable real set $\mathbb F$. Input $N=2^m$ with $m\ge0$, $x\in\mathbb C^N$ whose real and imaginary coordinates all belong to $\mathbb F$, a direction `forward` or `inverse`, an exact rational twiddle tolerance $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer exponent limits $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$ for the dyadic phase format, an initial phase precision $p_0\ge2$, a finite precision cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, a finite elementary-series cap $J\ge1$, and a maximum radix-two recursion depth $d_{\max}\ge0$. At precision $p$, phase endpoints use the dyadic format with precision $p$ and exponent limits $e_{\min},e_{\max}$. Output a vector in $\mathbb C^N$ and the certificate for each twiddle used, or the first `range-failure`/`inconclusive` status and its stage, index, or phase. Before multiplying by a certified phase $\widehat w_k$, require its real and imaginary coordinates to belong to $\mathbb F$; otherwise return `range-failure` at that twiddle index before performing the product. Use the same floating-point model instance throughout the recursion.

For direction `forward`, at $N=1$ return $x_0$. For $N>1$, if $d_{\max}=0$ return `inconclusive` with the `subdivision-cap-exhausted` status. Otherwise split $x$ into even and odd subsequences and recursively compute their unitary transforms $E,O$ by calling this routine with the same phase parameters and depth cap $d_{\max}-1$. For each $0\le k<N/2$, call [[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]] on $(q,\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J)$ with $q=-2k/N$, obtaining $(\widehat w_k,\epsilon_k)$ approximating $w_k=e^{-2\pi ik/N}$. Compute the six-real-operation complex product $t_k=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat w_kO_k)$, componentwise rounded sums $s_k^+=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(E_k+t_k)$ and $s_k^-=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(E_k-t_k)$, and $\widehat c=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt{1/2})$. Set output entries $k$ and $k+N/2$ to the componentwise rounded real scalings $\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat c s_k^+)$ and $\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat c s_k^-)$, respectively. For direction `inverse`, conjugate the input, run the forward routine with the same phase parameters and $d_{\max}$, and conjugate its output; conjugation is exact in the operationwise model. Propagate any failed phase certificate; on arithmetic failure return the operationwise range status and index. Accuracy is asserted only by the separate theorem and only on a successful no-range-failure execution.

Fix an instance of the operationwise floating-point model in [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], with representable real set $\mathbb F$. Input two finite complex sequences $a,b$ whose real and imaginary coordinates all belong to $\mathbb F$, a mode `cyclic` or `linear`, and phase/FFT controls: an exact rational twiddle tolerance $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer dyadic exponent limits $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$, an initial phase precision $p_0\ge2$, a finite precision cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, a finite elementary-series cap $J\ge1$, and a maximum radix-two recursion depth $d_{\max}\ge0$. At precision $p$, phase endpoints use the dyadic format with precision $p$ and exponent limits $e_{\min},e_{\max}$. In cyclic mode the inputs must have the same length $M=2^q$ with integer $q\ge0$; the requested exact operation is cyclic convolution on $\mathbb Z/M\mathbb Z$. In linear mode, with lengths $n,m\ge1$, set $L=n+m-1$, choose the least power of two $M\ge L$, and append zeros to both inputs to length $M$; the requested output is the first $L$ entries of their cyclic convolution. Validate the mode, positive dimensions, input representability, exact rational tolerance, integer control parameters and their displayed inequalities, and the cyclic power-of-two condition before any transform call. If any such input constraint fails, return `inconclusive` with diagnostic `invalid-input` and the offending parameter or coordinate, without a vector output. An arithmetic range failure returns `range-failure` with its operation and index, without a vector output.

For either mode, call [[alg-na-computed-unitary-radix-two-fft]] on each length-$M$ input with direction `forward` and the same $(\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J,d_{\max})$ controls. Multiply corresponding transform entries as $\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat A_k\widehat B_k)$ using the six-real-operation complex product of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Call the same FFT routine on this product vector with direction `inverse` and the same controls, and multiply each output component by the computed real scalar $\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt M)$ using componentwise rounded real scaling. Return the length-$M$ cyclic result, or its first $L$ entries in linear mode, only if every phase, recursion-budget, and arithmetic operation succeeds; otherwise return the first `inconclusive` or `range-failure` status and index. The exact convolution identity and numerical-error claim are separate results.

At each precision, let the representable set, normal range, and unit roundoff be an instance of [[def-standard-relative-floating-point-model-and-unit-roundoff]] specialized to a finite binary format of integer precision $p\ge2$ and integer normal-exponent bounds $j_{\min}\le j\le j_{\max}$. Its normal values are $\pm m2^{j-p+1}$ for integers $2^{p-1}\le m<2^p$ and $j_{\min}\le j\le j_{\max}$, with $N_{\min}=2^{j_{\min}}$ and $N_{\max}=(2^p-1)2^{j_{\max}-p+1}$. The rounding rule is round-to-nearest, ties-to-even by the parity of the normalized significand. Each precision in a mixed-precision procedure has its own format, range, and valid unit-roundoff bound. On every real exact result that is zero or normal, $\operatorname{fl}$ uses this rule; every other nonzero exact result (subnormal or overflow), NaN, infinity, invalid operation, or division by zero returns range-failure. A real add, subtract, multiply, or divide is one rounded operation. For positive in-range $x$, $\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt{x})$ is correctly rounded to nearest, ties-to-even, and fails unless its result is positive and normal. A real fused multiply-add returns the correctly rounded value of the single exact expression $ab+c$; it is not two operations.

Complex addition and subtraction round real and imaginary components separately. A complex product (a+ib)(c+id) uses four rounded real products ac, bd, ad, bc, then rounded subtraction and addition, for six real operations. Conjugation and sign changes are exact. Scaling and division by a positive real scalar round each complex component separately; no other complex division primitive is used here.

A procedure succeeds only when each exact intermediate is zero or normal and every rounded output is finite; otherwise it returns the first range-failure with its operation or pivot index. For ku<1 write gamma_k=ku/(1-ku). This is a no-underflow success model, not the gradual-underflow model.

Fix an instance of the operationwise floating-point model in [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], with representable real set $\mathbb F$. Input $N\ge1$, $x\in\mathbb C^N$ whose real and imaginary coordinates all belong to $\mathbb F$, an exact rational phase tolerance $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer dyadic exponent limits $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$, an initial phase precision $p_0\ge2$, a finite precision cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, a finite elementary-series cap $J\ge1$, and a maximum radix-two recursion depth $d_{\max}\ge0$. At precision $p$, phase endpoints use the dyadic format with precision $p$ and exponent limits $e_{\min},e_{\max}$. Before any certified phase is used as an arithmetic operand or stored in an input vector to a computed subroutine, require its real and imaginary coordinates to belong to $\mathbb F$; otherwise return `range-failure` with that phase index before the operation or subcall. Use the same floating-point model instance throughout all recursive calls. The output convention is the **unnormalised** DFT $X_k=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}x_je^{-2\pi ijk/N}$ ([[def-unnormalised-engineering-dft-and-conversion]]); the procedure returns an approximate vector or the first `inconclusive`/`range-failure` status.

1. For $N=1$, return $x_0$.
2. If $N=2^m$ with $m\ge1$, call [[alg-na-computed-unitary-radix-two-fft]] in `forward` mode with controls $(\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J,d_{\max})$ and multiply each output by the computed scalar $\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt N)$. A failed subcall or scale operation returns its status.
3. If $N$ is composite and not a power of two, find its least divisor $r$ with $1<r<N$ by trial division and put $s=N/r$. For $u=0,\ldots,r-1$, recursively call this procedure with the same controls on the strided vector $(x_{u+rv})_{v=0}^{s-1}$ to obtain an approximate unnormalised length-$s$ DFT $U_u$. For each $0\le k_2<s$ and $0\le u<r$, call [[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]] on $(q,\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J)$ with $q=-2uk_2/N$ to obtain the twiddle enclosure, then multiply its returned phase by $U_u(k_2)$ using $\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}$. For each $0\le k_2<s$, apply this procedure recursively, with the same controls, to the length-$r$ vector of these products indexed by $u$, and for every $0\le k_1<r$ store its output $k_1$ at index $k_2+sk_1$. Propagate any failed phase or arithmetic status.
4. If $N$ is prime, set $M$ to the least power of two with $M\ge2N-1$. For each $0\le j<N$, call [[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]] on $(q,\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J)$ with $q=-j^2/N$ to obtain $\widehat\alpha_j$, and set $a_j=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat\alpha_jx_j)$; set the remaining entries of $a\in\mathbb C^M$ to zero. For each $-(N-1)\le t\le N-1$, obtain $\widehat\beta_t$ by the same call with $q=t^2/N$ and set $b_{[t]_M}=\widehat\beta_t$, setting other entries of $b$ to zero. Compute the cyclic convolution with [[alg-na-computed-fft-cyclic-and-linear-convolution]] in `cyclic` mode using controls $(\tau,e_{\min},e_{\max},p_0,p_{\max},J,d_{\max})$. For each $0\le k<N$, obtain $\widehat\gamma_k$ by the same phase call with $q=-k^2/N$ and set $\widehat X_k=\operatorname{fl}_{\mathbb C}(\widehat\gamma_k\widehat c_k)$. Return the first $N$ entries or the first failure status.

The divisor search and phase-enclosure work have separate integer/interval budgets and are not counted as complex arithmetic operations in the operation-count theorem. The exact factorization lemmas and the chirp-phase error theorem state what is guaranteed; this procedure by itself makes no general mixed-radix stability claim.

For $P=1$ set $W_1(u)=\mathbf 1_{[0,1]}(u)$, including both endpoints. For an
integer $P\ge2$, define the causal order-$P$ window by
$$W_P(u)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac1{(P-1)!}\sum_{j=0}^{P}(-1)^j\binom Pj(u-j)_+^{P-1},&0\le u\le P,\\0,&u<0\text{ or }u>P.\end{cases}$$
Here $s_+=\max(s,0)$, $m!$ is the factorial of the nonnegative integer $m$
with $0!=1$, and for integers $0\le j\le P$,
$\binom Pj=P!/(j!(P-j)!)$. Convolution means the integral operation
$$(f*g)(u)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(u-s)g(s)\,ds,$$
when the integrand is measurable and integrable, as in
[[def-convolution-of-two-functions-on-rn]]. The displayed formula is finite at
every $u$ and directly defines $W_P$ to vanish outside $[0,P]$; the local
alias lemma proves that it agrees with the $P$-fold convolution of $W_1$ and
establishes the resulting integral, positivity, partition, Fourier-transform,
and derivative identities.

Fix neutral point-source data $(A,V,\Lambda,\kappa_k,(x_i,q_i)_{i=1}^n)$ from
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]], an Ewald parameter
$\alpha>0$, integers $M_1,M_2,M_3\ge1$, an assignment order $P\ge2$, and write
$N_g=M_1M_2M_3$. Let $\mathcal G=\prod_{r=1}^3\{0,\ldots,M_r-1\}$ and take
$W_P$ from [[def-ewald-causal-cardinal-spline-window]]. Define the periodic
causal assignment weights, for $t\in[0,1)^3$ and $\ell\in\mathcal G$, by
$$w_\ell(t)=\prod_{r=1}^3\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z} W_P(M_rt_r-\ell_r-jM_r).$$
The sums are finite because $W_P$ is supported on $[0,P]$. They collect every
support index into its grid residue; if $P>M_r$, distinct support indices that
wrap to the same residue are added. The spread grid is
$$g_\ell=\sum_{i=1}^n q_iw_\ell(t_i),\qquad t_i=A^{-1}x_i\pmod{\mathbb Z^3}.$$

Use the negative-sign unitary tensor DFT convention
$$\widehat g_M(k)=N_g^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}g_\ell e^{-2\pi i\sum_{r=1}^3k_r\ell_r/M_r},$$
which is the product transform of
[[def-unitary-discrete-fourier-transform-on-z-mod-n]]. Signed frequency
representatives are chosen before evaluating windows. A retained set
$\mathcal K\subset\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$ is finite, symmetric under
$k\mapsto-k$, injective modulo $(M_1,M_2,M_3)$, and satisfies
$|k_r|<M_r/2$ for each coordinate. In particular, even-grid Nyquist modes are
not silently retained.

For $u\in\mathbb R$, put $\operatorname{sinc}(u)=\sin(u)/u$ when $u\ne0$ and
$\operatorname{sinc}(0)=1$. Define
$$D(k)=\prod_{r=1}^3e^{-\pi iPk_r/M_r} \operatorname{sinc}(\pi k_r/M_r)^P.$$
Only modes with $D(k)\ne0$ are admissible for division. A computed
implementation must first certify a strictly positive lower bound for
$|D(k)|$; otherwise it returns `denominator-inconclusive` without dividing.
For $k\in\mathcal K$, define
$$a_k(t)=e^{-2\pi i k\cdot t},\quad b_k(t)=\frac{\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t) e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}}{\overline{D(k)}},\quad \rho_k=\sum_iq_i a_k(t_i),\quad z_k=\frac{\sqrt{N_g}\,\widehat g_M(k)}{\overline{D(k)}}.$$
The denominator is the complex conjugate of the printed window multiplier; this
sign is part of the definition. Set
$$c_k=\frac{4\pi}{V|\kappa_k|^2} e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}.$$
The exact retained reciprocal energy is
$$E_{\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|\rho_k|^2,$$
and the mesh reciprocal energy is
$$E_M=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|z_k|^2.$$

Let $\mathfrak d_k(t)$ be the declared physical mesh derivative: it is
$\nabla_xb_k(t)=A^{-T}\nabla_tb_k(t)$ wherever the classical derivative
exists. A grid knot is a point with $M_rt_r\in\mathbb Z$ for some coordinate
$r$. At a $P=2$ knot, take the one-sided vector limits from all adjacent open
mesh boxes. Define $\mathfrak d_k(t)$ to be any selected one-sided limit or the
arithmetic average of all those limits. This is a procedure value and does not
assert that the classical derivative exists there. The
energy-gradient mesh force is
$$F_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\overline{z_k}\mathfrak d_k(t_i)\right).$$
Define the diagonal mesh-self correction and corrected reciprocal energy by
$$C_M=\frac12\sum_iq_i^2\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k (|b_k(t_i)|^2-1),\qquad E_M^{\mathrm{corr}}=E_M-C_M.$$
Whether the declared force is the derivative of this corrected energy, and the
error bound it satisfies, are proved separately.

Use the periodic cardinal-assignment model of
[[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]], with integers $M_r\ge1$, order
$P\ge2$, grid size $N_g=\prod_rM_r$, a retained signed mode $k$ satisfying
$|k_r|<M_r/2$, and $D(k)\ne0$. Put $u_r=k_r/M_r$,
$a_k(t)=e^{-2\pi i k\cdot t}$, and
$$r_{k,n}=\prod_{r=1}^3 \frac{\overline{D_r(k_r+n_rM_r)}}{\overline{D_r(k_r)}},\qquad D_r(m)=e^{-\pi iPm/M_r}\operatorname{sinc}(\pi m/M_r)^P.$$
Then the single-particle assignment factor and the spread-grid coefficient obey
the absolutely convergent identities
$$b_k(t)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}r_{k,n}a_{k+n\odot M}(t),\qquad z_k=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}r_{k,n}\rho_{k+n\odot M},$$
where $(n\odot M)_r=n_rM_r$ and
$\rho_j=\sum_iq_i e^{-2\pi i j\cdot t_i}$. In particular
$$z_k-\rho_k=\sum_{n\ne0}r_{k,n}\rho_{k+n\odot M}.$$
The mesh coefficient also has the exact finite representation
$z_k=\sum_iq_i b_k(t_i)$, so no cell-volume or grid-size factor remains after
the displayed $\sqrt{N_g}$ conversion. The alias bound below uses only the Fourier series of
the compact spline; the lattice Poisson theorem is not applied to that spline.

For $u_r\ne0$ define
$$a_r(P,u_r)=\sum_{m\ne0}\left|\frac{u_r}{u_r+m}\right|^P, \qquad a_r(P,0)=0,\qquad A_k=\prod_{r=1}^3(1+a_r(P,u_r))-1.$$
Then $|b_k(t)-a_k(t)|\le A_k$, $|b_k(t)|\le1+A_k$, and
$|z_k-\rho_k|\le Q A_k$ for $Q=\sum_i|q_i|$. For $J\ge1$ and
$0<|u_r|<1/2$,
$$a_r(P,u_r)\le 2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\sum_{m=1}^\infty m^{-P},\qquad \sum_{|m|>J}\left|\frac{u_r}{u_r+m}\right|^P\le 2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\frac{\lfloor J\rfloor^{1-P}}{P-1}.$$
Thus every alias controller has a finite p-series remainder bound.
The periodic assignment also satisfies $\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t)=1$,
so the spread-grid zero mode is $\sum_{\ell}g_\ell=\sum_iq_i=0$ for neutral data.

Use the data and aliases of
[[lem-ewald-pme-spline-alias-and-dft-normalization]]. Write
$h_r(0)=1$ and, for $u_r=k_r/M_r\ne0$,
$h_r(n)=|u_r/(u_r+n)|^P$ for $n\ne0$; when $u_r=0$, set $h_r(n)=0$ for
$n\ne0$. Put
$$a_r=\sum_{n\ne0}h_r(n).$$
For $P\ge3$, define
$$v_r=\sum_{n\ne0}|k_r+nM_r|h_r(n),\qquad J_{k,r}=(|k_r|+v_r)\prod_{s\ne r}(1+a_s)-|k_r|,$$
and
$$B_k=2\pi\|A^{-T}\|_2\left(\sum_{r=1}^3J_{k,r}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
For $P\ge3$ the physical derivative alias error satisfies
$$\|\nabla_xb_k(t)-\nabla_xa_k(t)\|_2\le B_k.$$
Each series has a finite p-series controller: for $0<|u_r|<1/2$,
$$a_r\le2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\zeta(P),\qquad v_r\le2M_r\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^{P-1}}\zeta(P-1),$$
where $\zeta(s)=\sum_{m\ge1}m^{-s}$ for $s>1$. For $J_0\ge1$, after summing exactly over
$1\le|n|\le J_0$, the respective omitted tails are at most
$$2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\frac{\lfloor J_0\rfloor^{1-P}}{P-1},\qquad 2M_r\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^{P-1}}\frac{\lfloor J_0\rfloor^{2-P}}{P-2}.$$

For the approved $P=2$ case, the absolute derivative p-series above diverges
when $u_r\ne0$. Instead use the finite derivative of the local piecewise
window sum. At every open mesh box and each one-sided knot limit, put
$$C_{k,r}=\frac{2M_r}{|D(k)|}+2\pi|k_r|,\qquad B_k=\|A^{-T}\|_2\left(\sum_{r=1}^3C_{k,r}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
This is a computable finite bound for the same physical derivative error. At a
grid knot, use the declared $\mathfrak d_k(t)$ branch from
[[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]]: it is a selected one-sided value
or their average and obeys the bound, but is not asserted to be a classical
derivative there. Thus for the full $P\ge2$ range the bound is on
$\mathfrak d_k(t)-\nabla_xa_k(t)$, with $\mathfrak d_k=\nabla_xb_k$ wherever
the classical derivative exists.

Assume Countable Choice. For an invertible real $3\times3$ matrix $B$, put
$\Gamma=B\mathbb Z^3$ and
$$C_B=\bigl(2\|B^{-1}\|_2(1+\sqrt3\|B\|_2)+1\bigr)^3.$$
Here $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Euclidean operator norm. Uniformly over every
translate $y+\Gamma$ and every integer shell $m\ge0$,
$$\#\{z\in y+\Gamma:m\le|z|<m+1\}\le C_B(m+1)^3.$$

For $\beta>0$, any integer $p\ge0$, and integer $M\ge0$, set
$$T_p(\beta,M)=\sum_{m=M}^{\infty}(m+1)^p e^{-\beta m^2}.$$
For any integer $J\ge M$ satisfying $2\beta J(J+1)\ge p$, define
$$I_0(J,\beta)=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2\sqrt\beta}\operatorname{erfc}(\sqrt\beta J),\quad I_1(J,\beta)=\frac{e^{-\beta J^2}}{2\beta},$$
and recursively for $2\le s\le p$,
$$I_s(J,\beta)=\frac{J^{s-1}e^{-\beta J^2}}{2\beta} +\frac{s-1}{2\beta}I_{s-2}(J,\beta).$$
Then the finite controller
$$U_p(\beta,M,J)=\sum_{m=M}^{J}(m+1)^p e^{-\beta m^2} +\sum_{s=0}^{p}\binom ps I_s(J,\beta)$$
satisfies $T_p(\beta,M)\le U_p(\beta,M,J)$. Such a $J$ exists for every
$\beta>0$, $M\ge0$, and integer $p\ge0$.

Assume Countable Choice and a neutral finite point-source configuration on
$A\mathbb Z^3$ from [[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Fix
$\alpha>0$, real and reciprocal cutoffs $R,K_c\ge1$, a mesh with integers
$M_r\ge1$ and order $P\ge2$, and a finite symmetric retained set
$\mathcal K\subseteq\{k\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}:|\kappa_k|\le K_c\}$
that is injective modulo $(M_1,M_2,M_3)$ and has $|k_r|<M_r/2$ and $D(k)\ne0$
for every $k\in\mathcal K$. Put $Q=\sum_i|q_i|$ and let
$$\mathcal B_{K_c}=\{k\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}:|\kappa_k|\le K_c\},\qquad \mathcal M_{K_c}=\mathcal B_{K_c}\setminus\mathcal K.$$
This in-ball omitted set is finite. Write $M_R=\lfloor R\rfloor$,
$M_K=\lfloor K_c\rfloor$, $C_R=C_A$, and $C_K=C_{2\pi A^{-T}}$ for the shell
constants in [[lem-ewald-lattice-shell-gaussian-tail-controllers]]. Choose
integers $J_R\ge M_R$, $J_K\ge M_K$ such that
$2\alpha^2J_R(J_R+1)\ge3$ and
$\frac{1}{2\alpha^2}J_K(J_K+1)\ge3$. Let $U_3(\beta,M,J)$ be that supplier's
finite upper controller for $\sum_{m=M}^\infty(m+1)^3e^{-\beta m^2}$, and put
$$\begin{aligned} \overline B_R^U&=\frac{QC_R}{\sqrt\pi\alpha}U_3(\alpha^2,M_R,J_R),& \overline B_R^E&=\frac{Q^2C_R}{2\sqrt\pi\alpha}U_3(\alpha^2,M_R,J_R),& \overline B_R^{F,i}&=\frac{|q_i|QC_R}{\sqrt\pi}(2\alpha+\alpha^{-1})U_3(\alpha^2,M_R,J_R),\\ \overline B_K^U&=\frac{4\pi QC_K}{V}U_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K,J_K),& \overline B_K^E&=\frac{2\pi Q^2C_K}{V}U_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K,J_K),& \overline B_K^{F,i}&=\frac{4\pi|q_i|QC_K}{V}U_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K,J_K). \end{aligned}$$

For $\phi_s(r)=\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha r)/r$, define the finite real-space
potential at an off-source point by
$$S_R(x)=\sum_iq_i\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in\Lambda\\|x-x_i+\lambda|\le R}}\phi_s(|x-x_i+\lambda|),$$
and the finite real energy by
$$E_R=\frac12\sum_i\sum_j\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in\Lambda\\|x_i-x_j+\lambda|\le R}}'q_iq_j\phi_s(|x_i-x_j+\lambda|),$$
where the prime omits exactly $(j,\lambda)=(i,0)$. Let
$$F_{R,i}=-q_i\sum_{\substack{1\le j\le n,\ \lambda\in\Lambda\\(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0),\,|x_i-x_j+\lambda|\le R}}q_j\,\phi_s'(|x_i-x_j+\lambda|)\frac{x_i-x_j+\lambda}{|x_i-x_j+\lambda|}.$$
The cutoff index set is held fixed in this force sum; the cutoff indicator is
not differentiated. Set
$$\widetilde U(x)=S_R(x)+U_{M,\mathcal K}(x),$$
$$\widetilde E^\chi=E_R+E_{M,\mathcal K}^\chi-\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\sum_iq_i^2,\qquad \widetilde F_i^\chi=F_{R,i}+F_{M,i}^\chi,$$
where $\chi=\mathrm{uncorr}$ uses the uncorrected energy and force of
[[thm-ewald-pme-reciprocal-energy-force-error-bound]], and $\chi=\mathrm{corr}$ uses
its optional diagonal self-corrected branch. For the uncorrected branch suppose
the derivative/gather residuals are $H_k$; the corrected branch uses the
energy-gradient gather, so $H_k=0$.

Suppose the computed finite outputs $\widehat U(x),\widehat E^\chi,\widehat
F_i^\chi$ have certified arithmetic radii $\varepsilon_U,\varepsilon_E,
\varepsilon_{F,i}\ge0$ relative to $\widetilde U,\widetilde E^\chi,
\widetilde F_i^\chi$, respectively. Define
$$\begin{aligned} \eta_U={}&\overline B_R^U+\overline B_K^U+Q\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m+Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)+\varepsilon_U,\\ \eta_E^{\mathrm{uncorr}}={}&\overline B_R^E+\overline B_K^E+\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m+\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)+\varepsilon_E,\\ \eta_E^{\mathrm{corr}}={}&\overline B_R^E+\overline B_K^E+\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m+\frac{Q^2-\sum_iq_i^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)+\varepsilon_E,\\ \eta_{F,i}^{\mathrm{uncorr}}={}&\overline B_R^{F,i}+\overline B_K^{F,i}+|q_i|Q\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m|\kappa_m|+|q_i|Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k+(1+A_k)H_k]+\varepsilon_{F,i},\\ \eta_{F,i}^{\mathrm{corr}}={}&\overline B_R^{F,i}+\overline B_K^{F,i}+|q_i|Q\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m|\kappa_m|+|q_i|(Q-|q_i|)\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k]+\varepsilon_{F,i}. \end{aligned}$$
Then, for every off-source $x$ and each particle $i$,
$$|\widehat U(x)-U_\alpha(x)|\le\eta_U,\qquad |\widehat E^\chi-E|\le\eta_E^\chi,\qquad \|\widehat F_i^\chi-F_i\|_2\le\eta_{F,i}^\chi.$$
Here $U_\alpha,E,F_i$ are the exact mean-zero periodic Ewald potential,
renormalized energy, and particle force. The finite omitted-mode sums
$\mathcal M_{K_c}$ explicitly charge every mode in the radial ball that the
mesh did not retain, including Nyquist modes. Missing arithmetic radii do not
produce a certificate; no RMS estimate is substituted for these deterministic
bounds.

For the formal exact-constant work count, let $\mathsf N_{\mathrm{img}}$ be
the total number of candidate real-image indices inspected in the finite
potential, energy, and force loops, and let $\mathsf N_{\mathrm{cert}}$ be the
total number of mode and finite controller entries inspected in constructing
the omitted-mode ledger and error certificate. Count each such outer-loop
inspection as one work unit and count the transform arithmetic in the formal
exact-constant model of [[thm-na-arbitrary-length-fft-correctness-and-cost]].
For fixed $P$, the finite evaluation uses
$$O\!\left(N_g\log(2N_g)+nP^3+\mathsf N_{\mathrm{img}}+\mathsf N_{\mathrm{cert}}\right)$$
work units, with at most three tensor transforms before optional
mesh-self correction. The correction adds
$$O\!\left(N_g\log(2N_g)+nP^6\right)$$
when its cyclic kernel is precomputed. These counts do not include interval
precision, elementary-function evaluation, memory traffic, bit complexity, or
the transform subroutine's integer factor search and phase evaluation; no
operation count is used as an accuracy bound.

derivations.claim: Each non-transform request [F1] either returns its supplied certified data or consumes at most the positive finite $B_{\mathrm{encl}}$ instruction budget and exits. Each counted instruction on finite rational data or fixed-format operands terminates, with the model's range-failure outcome when appropriate. Thus no request can perform unbounded precision refinement, wait for an undecided equality, or search until a valid radius appears. Initial validation uses finitely many particle pairs and scalar/integer conditions. It either exits with a declared status, or supplies the finite data needed by the first step.

A phase call has at most $p_{\max}-p_0+1$ precision attempts by [F2]. At each attempt the Machin sums have $J_{\mathrm{phase}}+1$ terms and rational tails. Its elementary DAGs are finite. Topological sorting removes a node at each successful iteration or reports a cycle, so it finishes. For every finite positive-endpoint logarithm interval, only finitely many dyadic bins lie between its endpoints; arctangent uses at most seven fixed pieces. For sine/cosine the algorithm computes finite $K=\lceil2M_X/p_-\rceil+1$ when $p_->0$ and examines only $-K,\ldots,K$, otherwise returning a status. Every series has its fixed truncation degree; the exponential squaring count is the finite integer $\max(0,e_{\max}+2)$. Square-root endpoint bisection starts with integer gap $2^{p+1}$ and at each iteration replaces it by at most its ceiling half, so at most $p+1$ iterations suffice. Directed conversion of a rational endpoint searches a finite representable set using integer comparisons. All other rational endpoint arithmetic terminates, and unresolved domains or nonfinite conversions return statuses. Therefore each elementary call and each capped phase call terminates, including when its requested phase tolerance is unmet.

Induction on the integer $d_{\max}$ proves termination of each radix-two call: length one returns directly, depth zero at larger length returns inconclusive, and otherwise its two children have depth $d_{\max}-1$. Each finite butterfly list uses only scalar operations and the terminating phase calls of step 1.2. An inverse call adds only two finite conjugations around its forward call. Hence a radix-two call has a finite binary recursion tree, of at most $2^{d_{\max}+1}-1$ nodes. A cyclic convolution has just three such calls and a finite list of products/scalings, so it terminates too.

In Step 1 of the evaluator, obtaining the finite bound $B_K$ either succeeds in bounded work or exits by step 1.1. Its outward endpoint has an exactly computable integer ceiling $N_K$. The box has $(2N_K+1)^3$ integer triples; each distance/cutoff decision uses a bounded request and either includes, excludes, or returns cutoff-inconclusive. Retained-mode restrictions are finite integer comparisons. Thus both the retained set and omitted-mode ledger are constructed in finite work. Their symmetry, strict mesh restrictions and injection modulo the mesh are preserved because successful comparisons certify the exact radial membership: two strictly interior signed representatives differing by a mesh multiple must coincide coordinatewise.

In Step 2, if an assignment-coordinate interval has width greater than one, the stated exit occurs. Otherwise its integer support endpoints are finite, and the interval from $a^- -P$ to $a^+$ has length at most $P+1$. Any interval of length at most $P+1$ contains at most $P+2$ integers, so the triple list has at most $(P+2)^3$ entries. The finite formula for $W_P$ in [F5] uses integer powers, factorials, binomial coefficients, and $P+1$ summands, all finite for the given integer $P$. Each arithmetic/enclosure request terminates by step 1.1. Reduction modulo each positive $M_r$ and accumulation keep duplicate wraps rather than starting another loop. The same proof applies to the optional query support and to the finite polynomial derivatives. If a $P=2$ selected right-hand box cannot be certified within its budget, the explicit arithmetic-inconclusive branch returns; an exact knot certificate selects the same one-sided derivative in both correction factors.

In Step 6 the bounded request for $B_R$ either exits or gives a finite ceiling $N_R$. For each needed pair the box has $(2N_R+1)^3$ candidates. There are at most $n$ query/source pairs and $n^2$ particle pairs for each of the energy and force sums. For a true retained image, $|t_a-t_b|\le\sqrt3$ gives $|\ell|\le\|A^{-1}\|_2R+\sqrt3\le B_R$, so the box misses none. Each candidate uses a bounded include/exclude/cutoff-inconclusive test. The own zero-image term is omitted before singular kernel evaluation; every other kernel division requires a certified positive distance bound or exits. Its elementary values and finite derivative arithmetic use step 1.1. The real potential, energy, force and ordinary Ewald self constant thus finish, without differentiating the cutoff indicator.

For arbitrary transform length $N$, trial division can examine $2,\ldots,N-1$ and thus terminates. A composite non-power-of-two branch has factors $1<r,s<N$, makes $r$ length-$s$ calls and $s$ length-$r$ calls, and a finite twiddle list. Strong induction on $N$ proves these calls terminate, with length one the base case. A power of two uses step 2.1. At a prime, start at one and double until the padding length is at least $2N-1$. This search is finite since $2^j\ge j+1$ by integer induction, and its least resulting power $M$ satisfies $M<4N$. There are finitely many chirp phases, one cyclic convolution of length $M$, and finitely many final products; steps 1.2 and 2.1 finish them. Thus all transform calls terminate with their actual supplied caps; no sufficient-depth or phase-success assumption is needed.

Step 7's floor requests terminate or return cutoff-inconclusive. With determined floors, [F6] constructs the real controller using $J_R-M_R+1$ summands and the reciprocal controller using $J_K-M_K+1$ summands, plus four $I_s$ terms apiece. The $I_s$ recurrence reduces $s$ by two and stops at zero or one; no search for larger $J_R,J_K$ is performed. For each of finitely many retained modes, each one-dimensional source/derivative alias sum through $1\le|j|\le J_A$ has $2J_A$ terms, followed by the explicit p-series remainder. Their tensor products need no infinite summation; even a direct finite triple list would have at most $(2J_A+1)^3$ entries. For $P=2$, [F5] instead supplies the finite derivative-window bound. The omitted ledger is finite by step 2.2. All controller elementary values, arithmetic radii and final sums are bounded requests under step 1.1. This proves finite construction or an explicit arithmetic-inconclusive exit.

The full grid has finite size $N_g=M_1M_2M_3$. Each tensor transform has exactly $N_g/M_r$ coordinate fibers in direction $r$; every one-dimensional call terminates by step 3.1. Step 3 uses one tensor transform; Step 5 uses at most one potential transform, one force transform, and one optional kernel transform. Thus there are at most four tensor transforms, with finitely many normalizations. Failed calls/scales return transform-inconclusive; bounded denominator certification in Step 4 returns denominator-inconclusive before an unsafe division. Retained-mode and grid array construction are finite. All gathers visit the finite supports from step 2.3, and self correction visits at most $(P+2)^6$ ordered tuple pairs per particle. These polynomial products, derivatives and finite sums therefore terminate while retaining the same energy, force, and diagonal correction formulas.

Finally there are finitely many requested output radii and tolerance comparisons. Each is bounded by [F1]; proven satisfaction gives certified, proven excess gives certified-over-tolerance, and an unresolved decision returns arithmetic-inconclusive. Steps 1.1–3.2 prove that every preceding branch or subcall finishes; their finite concatenation therefore terminates with the stated record. Divisor, branch and enclosure checks prevent undefined successful outputs. On a valid final-output branch the unchanged arithmetic-enclosure assumptions and finite formulas meet [F7], so its potential, energy, force and optional self-correction error guarantees apply. No work-count premise was used to infer termination.

risk_review.notes: Reviewed all ten authored steps and complete current definitions of phase, elementary-DAG evaluator, dyadic square root/rounding, radix-two FFT, convolution, arbitrary-length transform and operationwise arithmetic. Non-transform programs have an instruction cap including control flow. Phase precision/series loops and trigonometric cell lists are finite; bisection gaps halve in at most p+1 iterations. Radix-two depth decreases, composite factors are strictly smaller, prime padding doubles finitely and invokes capped radix-two convolution. Integer norm boxes and supports give the claimed finite counts, including duplicate wraps and n=0. Controller recurrence decreases by two and alias truncations use fixed indices. No unresolved comparison retries internally. Final successful outputs invoke the conditional total certificate only after termination, with actual outward errors. No tolerance-achievability or stability conclusion is inferred from formal counts. No defect found. Reader/refuter have no findings.
